title: Inter Milan coach has a sly dig at Juventus
description: Juventus take on AC Milan this evening, while Inter Milan took on Napoli, giving us two important clashes between clubs expected to compete for the Serie A title this season.The Bianconeri will be kee...
fullText:
Juventus take on AC Milan this evening, while Inter Milan took on Napoli, giving us two important clashes between clubs expected to compete for the Serie A title this season.

The Bianconeri will be keen to win their fixture, but their supporters are also interested in the result between Inter Milan and Napoli, which ended in an Inter win. With four clubs expected to challenge for the title, both matches could have an impact on the race for the top spot.

Cristian Chivu won the league title with Inter last season, while Juventus finished outside the top four. AC Milan also failed to finish among the Champions League places, meaning neither of the clubs meeting tonight achieved the position expected of them.

Juve, Milan, Napoli and Inter Milan are certainly among the teams expected to compete for the league title this term. However, Como and Roma both finished above Juventus and Milan in the league table last season.

That explains why Como and Roma will compete in the Champions League while Juventus and Milan will not. Chivu appears to have used that fact to question whether the meeting between the Bianconeri and Milan should truly be considered a head-to-head clash for the title.

The Inter manager has challenged the idea that traditional status should determine which matches are regarded as important title clashes. His comments suggest that last season's standings should also be considered when assessing the importance of these fixtures.

Juventus and Milan have the history and reputation to be considered major rivals, but Chivu believes the definition of a head-to-head meeting should be based on more than tradition.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Chivu made his point clearly when discussing the weekend's fixtures. He said via Tuttosport:

"What does head-to-heads mean? Those against the top four in the table or traditional matches? Because Milan and Juventus finished so far behind last year, so what kind of head-to-head is it? I'm asking to understand. Are Juve and Milan head-to-heads? Then let's talk about tradition, otherwise Como is also a head-to-head."

His comments are likely to add another layer of interest to an already important weekend. Juventus and Milan will now have the chance to respond on the pitch.

title: Sources explain how Xabi Alonso persuaded Morgan Rogers to choose Chelsea
description: Morgan Rogers was Chelsea’s big addition this summer, and the story of how he came to Stamford Bridge is an interesting one.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a...
fullText:
Morgan Rogers was Chelsea's big addition this summer, and the story of how he came to Stamford Bridge is an interesting one.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Chelsea play Arsenal today in their first top 6 clash of the season, a perfect time to point out how close Morgan Rogers was to going to the Gunners before the Blues made the decisive move.

Simon Johnson's piece for the Athletic is all about that – he traces the transfer all the way back to two years ago, when Chelsea were first interested but ended up losing out to Aston Villa, who were already deep in negotiations with Middlesbrough.

Morgan Rogers (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

The whole piece is worth a read, but we were especially interested in what persuaded Rogers to pick Chelsea when he knew Arsenal were interested. A big part of it, apparently, was Xabi Alonso.

"[Rogers] came away from their conversation thinking Xabi Alonso is the real deal," a source at Chelsea said of the discussions between the two.

Alonso's passion was part of it, as was his detailed tactical plan for how he was going to use the 23 year old. Meanwhile Arsenal stuck to their £80m valuation. Chelsea weren't afraid to blow past that – we will soon find out who made the right call on that one.

Gary Neville is making big claims about Chelsea this season, saying that we've already got a better attack than Arsenal after our summer upgrades.

Also on Sky's pre game, Daniel Sturridge was backing Chelsea big time this year. But he knows a weakness that could stop them challenging for the title.

title: Horse that ran in Saratoga stakes race euthanized
description: Marvelous Madison, who finished fifth in the Yaddo on Aug. 30 at Saratoga, was euthanized due to a displaced fracture in her left hind leg.
fullText:
A 4-year-old filly died earlier this week after competing in a stakes race at Saratoga Race Course, after the horse was found to have suffered a fracture that left her unable to put her full weight on her left hind leg.

According to the state Gaming Commission's Equine Death and Breakdown Database, Marvelous Madison, who was trained by Jorge Abreu, was returned to her barn after finishing fifth in the Yaddo Stakes over Saratoga's Mellon turf course on Aug. 30. In the barn, Marvelous Madison became "toe touching lame in the left hind leg," meaning the filly was hesitant to put her full weight on the affected leg.

According to the Gaming Commission database, further evaluation of Marvelous Madison "revealed a displaced fracture." Because of the "poor prognosis," the database states, Marvelous Madison was euthanized.

The 4-year-old Marvelous Madison ran seven times in her career, with four of those races - including both of her career victories - coming at Saratoga. Earlier this summer at Saratoga, she won an allowance race on July 26 in her first race since August 2025.

On the state database, Marvelous Madison's injury and death were listed as "other" in the description of the incident, rather than being specifically racing- or training-related.

Since the 2026 summer meet began on July 3, the state database has listed three other fatalities, all training-related.

On Aug. 28, Stirring Words, a 3-year-old colt trained by Cherie DeVaux, "staggered" and "collapsed on the track surface" while warming up for a workout, according to the state database. The report noted that Stirring Words "suffered a cardiac event (and) expired."

On July 19, Magic Chuck, a 2-year-old trained by Whit Beckman, was pulled up during a breeze on Saratoga's Oklahoma training track. The horse was examined by a doctor, who determined that Magic Chuck had suffered a left scapula fracture. The colt was subsequently euthanized.

An unnamed 2-year-old trained by Todd Pletcher "collapsed and died" on July 4 when the horse was being pulled up by an exercise rider during a gallop on the main track.

Three other horses have been euthanized due to training-related injuries since April, when Saratoga's Oklahoma training track opened for the year.

On June 29, No Doubt About It, a 3-year-old gelding trained by Wesley Ward, was euthanized after the horse "flipped over and upon standing was immediately non-weight bearing," according to the Gaming Commission database.

On May 29, Shiny New Object, trained by Chad Brown, was euthanized after being pulled up at the ⅞ pole on the Oklahoma track. Shiny New Object was diagnosed with a humeral fracture and euthanized on the track.

On April 24, an unnamed 2-year-old colt trained by Melanie Giddings was euthanized after being diagnosed with a tibial fracture after the horse had last breezed on the Oklahoma track.

The 2026 racing season at Saratoga concludes Monday.

There's more to Albany with the Times Union.

title: Umpire Doug Eddings apologizes to Cardinals pitcher Hansel Rincon for telling him to straighten crooked cap
description: Eddings stopped play in the middle of an at-bat during Friday's game to tell the rookie hurler to fix his tilted cap.
fullText:
Umpire Doug Eddings apologized to St. Louis Cardinals pitcher Hancel Rincon on Saturday for telling the rookie to straighten his tilted cap during Friday's 7-6 win over the Colorado Rockies.

Eddings' directive to Rincon caused an uproar that resulted in Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol being ejected from the game for arguing over what occurred.

"He apologized for what happened [Friday] night," Rincon said through bullpen catcher and team interpreter Kleininger Teran, via the St. Louis Post Dispatch's Derrick Goold. "He also told me good luck for the rest of my career as a big-leaguer."

The rookie added that he told Eddings, "'Don't worry, it's nothing personal, and everything stays here," according to MLB.com's Owen Perkins.

Umpire Doug Eddings went on a power trip during the bottom of the 6th in the Cardinals Rockies game.

First, he demanded that pitcher Hancel Rincon (in his MLB debut) straighten his hat since no one will wear a hat like that on "his field".

When manager Oli Marmol went to talk… pic.twitter.com/ei4rCAalxq

The incident in question occurred during the sixth inning of Friday's game as Rincon made his major-league debut. As the rookie was pitching to Colorado's Cole Carrigg, Eddings called timeout and appeared to tell Rincon (through Cardinals catcher Leo Bernal) to straighten the brim of his cap.

Rincon had already given up a triple to TJ Rumfield and thrown a wild pitch that allowed the Rockies first baseman to score. Following Eddings' stoppage, the right-hander then threw a 96 mph fastball right down the middle of the strike zone that Carrigg hit off the wall in right-center field for an eventual inside-the-park home run.

After that, Rincon allowed a single to Connor Norby and he was replaced by Justin Bruihl. He finished with three runs and three hits allowed in 1/3 of an inning. As Bruihl warmed up, Marmol came out to argue with Eddings and was ejected from the game.

The Cardinals players are wearing their hats crooked tonight

Last night Doug Eddings demanded that pitcher Hancel Rincon (in his MLB debut) straighten out his hat pic.twitter.com/EVSFXgIXob

Following the game, Eddings told reporters that Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman raised the issue of Rincon's cap, asking if it could be worn that way. The umpire acknowledged that Rincon was not breaking any MLB rule. However, Goodman denied saying anything.

"I never once mentioned the hat," Goodman said, via MLB.com's Thomas Harding. "It doesn't matter who's pitching. I don't care how they wear the hat. I'm trying to find out where the ball is coming out, and I'm trying to worry about what I'm doing in the box. I'm not worried about how his hat looks."

O árbitro Doug Edding vou pedir desculpas a Hancel Rincon (estreiante na MLB) pela noite anterior.

Eu sinceramente não sei o que se passou na cabeça do Edding, um cara super experiente de Major, já viu vários usar o boné dessa forma e nunca teve essa atitude antes.

Bom,… https://t.co/PChUrnH4PB pic.twitter.com/lQL0IUH415

Before Saturday's game, which St. Louis lost 10-7, Eddings talked to Marmol and Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer, then made sure to speak with Rincon as the Cardinals pitchers walked to the bullpen.

During batting practice, most of the Cardinals players wore their caps with the brim turned to the left in protest. Many of them continued to wear their caps crooked, as did several Rockies players, during the game. Several Cardinals fans behind home plate and radio broadcaster John Rooney also wore their caps with a crooked brim in solidarity.

"I felt big support from my teammates," Rincon said. "Obviously, when you are together, like this group, we're gonna be much better."

Rincon also pitched in Saturday's game, allowing four runs and two hits in one inning. In addition to inspiring a fashion statement during his brief MLB career, the rookie has compiled a 47.25 ERA in his two outings.

title: Everton vs Manchester United Preview: Trouble Looms as Red Devils Chase Another Big Win
description: Everton host Manchester United at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday, September 6, in an early Premier League test for both teams. Everton enter the Everton vs Manchester United clash unbeaten after two league games, while Manchester United hope to build on their 5-2 win over Ipswich Town.David Moyes has helped Everton make a steady start, […] The post Everton vs Manchester United Preview: Trouble Looms as Red Devils Chase Another Big Win appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Everton host Manchester United at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday, September 6, in an early Premier League test for both teams. Everton enter the Everton vs Manchester United clash unbeaten after two league games, while Manchester United hope to build on their 5-2 win over Ipswich Town.

David Moyes has helped Everton make a steady start, with four points from their opening two matches. Michael Carrick's Manchester United have three points after losing to Hull on opening day.

The Everton vs Manchester United fixture also gives United a chance to improve their away form. Everton will rely on their strong defense, while Manchester United will look to Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha for attacking threat.

Everton have four points from their first two Premier League games after beating Leeds United and drawing 1-1 with Bournemouth. However, the club endured a busy transfer deadline day, including Iliman Ndiaye's departure. Christian Nørgaard remains Everton's only confirmed absentee because of a persistent groin injury.

David Moyes is expected to use a compact 4-2-3-1 formation. James Tarkowski and Jarrad Branthwaite are expected to play a key role in dealing with Manchester United's attacking players.

Manchester United responded to their opening-day defeat against Hull by beating Ipswich 5-2. Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick in that match and will again be central to United's attacking plans.

Manuel Ugarte remains out after surgery related to a World Cup injury. Amad Diallo is a major doubt, while Matthijs de Ligt and Mason Mount continue their return to full fitness.

Manchester United are expected to keep the same defensive structure. Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martínez and Luke Shaw should start in front of goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Matheus Cunha is expected to lead the attack.

Everton are expected to keep their 4-2-3-1 shape, with Moyes looking for defensive stability against Manchester United. Tarkowski and Branthwaite should form the center-back partnership.

The Everton vs Manchester United match comes with different pressures for both sides. Everton want to protect their unbeaten start, while Manchester United want consecutive league wins after their five-goal victory.

Manchester United have the stronger historical record in the Everton vs Manchester United fixture. United have won 97 of the 217 previous meetings between the clubs.

Everton have also struggled to beat Manchester United at home in recent league meetings. The Toffees have failed to win their last four home Premier League games against United.

Manchester United won the most recent meeting at Everton, securing a 1-0 victory in February 2026.

The match will take place at 2 p.m. BST at Hill Dickinson Stadium, with John Brooks appointed as referee. Sky Sports Main Event and Premier League will show the game in the UK, while USA Network will carry it in the United States.

fullText:
As we turn the page to September, we must take a moment to acknowledge the performance of these AL East leading Rays, and to do so we asked in this week's poll who the top performer was in August.

The choice was a difficult one! Among the five players suggested, only reliever Kevin Kelly did not accumulate any votes.

Baker held a 1.54 ERA across 12 appearances and 11⅔ innings in August, converting all nine of his save opportunities, allowed just eight hits and two walks while striking out 15, and kept the damage limited even on the rare nights things got interesting. Those nine saves helped push his season total to an MLB-leading 39 by the end of the month, and they extended a franchise-record consecutive saves streak that had already blown past Fernando Rodney's mark earlier in August. He also, notably, pitched three nights in a row toward the end of the month, a remarkable feat of availability.

Can Baker and the Rays hold their own down the stretch? Baker was pulled from his most recent pitching performance due to illness, and Shane McClanahan and Garrett Cleavinger both hit the injured list, but the Rays have promoted Ty Johnson, adding a fresh face and new look.

title: Cam Leiter helps Great Lakes clinch playoff berth
description: The Great Lakes Loons are the third Dodgers affiliate to clinch a postseason spot in 2026, along with Double-A Tulsa and Class-A Ontario. Player of the day Three starts into his Midwest League experience, and Cam Leiter has yet to allow an earned run. The right-hander pitched five scoreless innings on Saturday night to help […]
fullText:
The Great Lakes Loons are the third Dodgers affiliate to clinch a postseason spot in 2026, along with Double-A Tulsa and Class-A Ontario.

Three starts into his Midwest League experience, and Cam Leiter has yet to allow an earned run. The right-hander pitched five scoreless innings on Saturday night to help Great Lakes clinch a postseason berth, with three strikeouts, no walks, and only three singles allowed.

Leiter, drafted in the second round in 2025 out of Florida State, has allowed only one unearned run 11 1/3 innings, with 14 strikeouts. Between Class-A and High-A this season, Leiter has a 2.45 ERA and 30.9-percent strikeout rate in 55 innings in his professional debut.

The Comets won a low-scoring game in extra innings for a second straight day, this time besting the Round Rock Express (Rangers) in 11 innings. Ryan Fitzgerald's sacrifice fly drove home the game-winner.

Charlie Barnes pitched five scoreless innings in his start. Rehabber Jake Cousins allowed the only Round Rock run in his inning of work.

Ben Casparius started a new rehab assignment with a scoreless inning of work, his first appearance in 17 days after getting shut down with arm fatigue.

Paul Gervase pitched the final two innings in scoreless fashion, stranding the free runner in both frames to close out the win.

Chris Newell, who was promoted from Tulsa on Friday, played in his first Triple-A game on Saturday, and made an immediate impact with this game-ending gem.

ARE YOU SERIOUS?!

IN HIS FIRST GAME WITH OKC, CHRIS NEWELL MAKES ONE OF THE BEST PLAYS OF THE YEAR TO END THE GAME! pic.twitter.com/XxoqHuxhtH

The Drillers had big innings in the sixth and seventh, then held on to beat the Wichita Wind Surge (Twins). With 814 runs scored on the season, Tulsa set a record for the 50-year-old franchise, surpassing the 2000 team, a Texas Rangers affiliate that scored 806 runs in 140 games.

Jake Gelof already homered three times in this series, and on Saturday drove in three more runs with a double and single, giving him nine RBI through the first five games against Wichita. What a way to make a living.

Jake Gelof doubles and Sirota and Hainline score🔥 pic.twitter.com/miPeJwOv29

Logan Wagner and Sean McLain homered in the win.

Patrick Copen allowed three runs in his six innings, all three runs coming in the final frame. That briefly had Tulsa behind, but they rallied for three runs in the sixth and four runs in the seventh to put the game to bed.

Great pitching and patience allowed the Loons to beat the Lake County Captains (Guardians), and clinch the second half of the Midwest League East Division. Great Lakes is back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023.

Charles Davalan singled then stolen second base, and took third on a flyball single by Nico Perez. Then four Loons walked in the frame, with free passes to Eduardo Guerrero, Mairo Martinus, and Victor Rodrigues all bringing home runs.

After Leiter's five frames, Great Lakes got scoreless innings from Maddux Bruns and Matt Lanzendorfer before Dilan Figueredo entered with two runners on with nobody out in the eighth and pitched two scoreless innings to close out the clincher.

The Tower Buzzers scored seven runs in the fourth inning, allowed six runs in the seventh and two in the eighth, but then rallied for three runs with two outs in the ninth inning to stun the Rancho Cucamonga Quakes (Angels).

Down two runs and down to their last out, Ontario had two runners on base in the ninth. Francisco Espinoza singled to pull the Tower Buzzers within a run, the a hit by pitch and walk tied things up. Ching-Hsien Ko delivered the walk-off single, his second hit of the game.

Easton Shelton hit his California League-leading 37th home run in that fourth inning, a grand slam.

#Dodgers 1B prospect Easton Shelton his a 503-foot grand slam for his 37th homer of the year

He’s now broken Ryan Ward’s single-season Dodger prospect home run record pic.twitter.com/srUFfByHeL

Kellon Lindsey and Oswaldo Osorio homered for Ontario on Saturday. Osorio also walked twice and doubled, reaching base four times.

Charlie West, seventh-round draft pick this year out of UConn, struck out six and walked none in his four-inning start with two runs allowed.

Triple-A: Bobby Miller ended his rehab and was activated by the Dodgers. Reliever Kyle Hurt was optioned to Oklahoma City. Outfielder Alek Thomas was designated for assignment.

Double-A: Right-hander Angel Cruz was added to Tulsa's roster from the Arizona Complex League as an extra arm.

title: ‘When You Drinking, Nothing Really Good Comes From It’ — Pro Bowler Reacts to Mark Sanchez’s Guilty Plea Plan in Stabbing Incident
description: Mark Sanchez’s legal saga took a significant turn last week when the former NFL quarterback and ex-Fox Sports analyst filed a motion to plead guilty to charges stemming from an October 2025 altercation with a truck driver in Indianapolis. Sanchez faced a felony battery charge and three misdemeanors, including public intoxication and unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, after the alcohol-fueled confrontation left both him and 69-year-old Perry Tole seriously injured.
fullText:
Mark Sanchez's legal saga took a significant turn last week when the former NFL quarterback and ex-Fox Sports analyst filed a motion to plead guilty to charges stemming from an October 2025 altercation with a truck driver in Indianapolis.

Sanchez faced a felony battery charge and three misdemeanors, including public intoxication and unauthorized entry of a motor vehicle, after the alcohol-fueled confrontation left both him and 69-year-old Perry Tole seriously injured.

The guilty plea came just five days before his jury trial was set to begin, and former Pro Bowl wide receiver T.J. Houshmandzadeh, who has known Sanchez since he was a teenager, shared his reaction to the news.

Sanchez had been in Indianapolis to call the Raiders-Colts game for Fox on Oct. 5, 2025, when, in the early morning hours of Oct. 4, prosecutors say he accosted Tole in an alley between two downtown hotels while the truck driver was collecting used cooking oil.

The encounter escalated as Tole stabbed Sanchez in self-defense and was not charged, and both men were hospitalized. Fox Sports fired Sanchez in November and replaced him with Drew Brees.

The guilty plea, filed in Marion County Superior Court, requested that the judge vacate the Sept. 8 trial date and schedule a sentencing hearing. It remains unclear which specific charges Sanchez is pleading guilty to, and a judge still needs to formally accept the plea.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

Houshmandzadeh, a former Cincinnati Bengals wideout who made the Pro Bowl in 2007, expressed sympathy for Sanchez while acknowledging alcohol's role in the incident.

"It's just unfortunate," Houshmandzadeh said. "It was an unfortunate situation for Mark because I've known Mark since he was a teenager… Great person. So when I saw this, I was like, 'Mark Sanchez did this?' It shocked me. And so, when you drinking, I guess nothing really good comes from it. And so the good thing is Mark is okay. The gentleman that he 'assaulted' is okay. At least I believe he's okay."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Houshmandzadeh also offered his take on the logic behind pleading guilty when the evidence is difficult to dispute.

"If it's on video, what am I pleading not guilty for?" he added. "You see it clear as day. You see pictures of the injuries, and so you don't want to have to relive that moment. Neither one of those guys want to have to relive that moment. Now, what does that entail, though, by me pleading guilty, what does that entail?"

"I got probation? Do I get community service?" Houshmandzadeh continued. "Because if it entails that I got to go to jail, and I've never really been in jail, oh, I'm not pleading guilty. I'm going to go ahead and press my luck. So, I would assume it's just going to be some probation, some things he's going to have to do community service-wise, and he'll do that no problem."

The plea deal appears to be part of a broader effort to resolve both the criminal and civil cases simultaneously. Tole has a pending civil lawsuit against Sanchez and Fox Sports, and his attorney Matt Golitko said the two sides are on "a positive path toward an agreement."

NFL insider Mike Florio noted recently that in cases like these, a civil settlement often shapes the criminal outcome, explaining that when a victim is "placated by, for example, a sizable settlement of the civil case," prosecutors are more likely to allow a plea that doesn't involve jail time.

Fox Sports has moved on with Brees in the analyst role alongside play-by-play voice Adam Amin, but the broadcasting world hasn't entirely closed its doors on Sanchez.

If the criminal case ends with probation and community service, and the civil suit reaches an amicable resolution, a return to television isn't out of the question. It won't be at Fox, at least not anytime soon, but Sanchez's decade of NFL experience and three years in the broadcasting booth give him a foundation to rebuild from once the off-field issues are put to rest.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Arsenal vs. Chelsea match thread: old friends meet in a London derby
description: Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates in the first clash between traditional big four (or five, or six, however you want to phrase it) clubs of the Premier League season. In life, you’re either a red or a blue. Arsenal vs. Chelsea is about as red vs. blue as they come.
fullText:
Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates in the first clash between traditional big four (or five, or six, however you want to phrase it) clubs of the Premier League season. In life, you're either a red or a blue. Arsenal vs. Chelsea is about as red vs. blue as they come. This will be the first meeting between Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso, notable because the pair are lifelong friends. They played on teams growing up together in Spain.

Both clubs have two wins from two to start the season. Arsenal have done it with organization and defense, as you'd expect. They've not conceded a goal from either match (Hull City haven't conceded from three). Chelsea's attack has started the season quickly with seven goals scored from their opening two matches. They've also conceded five over those games, looking particularly vulnerable to crosses and set pieces.

Many expected new manager Xabi Alonso to setup his side to have plenty of the ball, as he did in previous coaching stops. In last weekend's 4-3 win over Brighton, Chelsea had 25% possession and completed just over 200 passes to Brighton's 590. The Blues attack quickly and directly. I'll be interested to see how they match up against Arsenal's more robust defense and organization.

Arsenal are unbeaten in 11 straight matches in all competitions against Chelsea (8-3-0). The Blues last win against the Gunners came in August 2022. There will be just two players starting for their same teams from the starting lineups that day — Reece James and Bukayo Saka. Kai Havertz is also likely to start but, as we know, switched sides in the interim. The Arsenal lineup from that match, woo boy — Leno, Cedric, Holding, Mari, Tierney, Xhaka, Lokonga, Saka, Smith Rowe, Pepe, Martinelli.

I'll be keeping a close watch on Bukayo Saka, who has scored in both matches this season for Arsenal but has a pretty dismal record against Chelsea. He'll no longer be running at Marc Cucurella, who like him or not, rate him or not, always did well keeping Saka quiet. Chelsea's defense has looked unorganized way more often than Xabi Alonso would like, so if there ever was a time for Bukayo to improve his output against the Blues, it'd be today.

Arsenal will be without William Saliba and Jurrien Timber, who remain out with the back and groin problems that have kept him out all season. The Dutch fullback is getting closer to making his return. Cristhian Mosquera, who was withdrawn against Aston Villa as a precaution per Mikel Arteta, looks like he'll miss out today. Bruno Guimaraes has been dealing with a groin issue and reportedly picked up an additional knock on the training ground this week but was with the squad for Sunday's pre-match walk. Declan Rice was a surprise miss from said walk. He trained all week, including yesterday, so his absence is particularly odd. UPDATE: Declan Rice starts today, he's fine.

For Chelsea, Moises Caicedo faces a late fitness test to determine his availability. He made a brief appearance as a substitute last week. New signing Marco Palestra, who played plenty in the preseason, has yet to make his Premier League debut for the club because of a knock. His status is up in the air / doubtful. Striker Emmanuel Emegha, who also joined the club this summer, is out with a hamstring issue. Jordan Henderson is still recovering from the broken arm / wrist he suffered at the World Cup after falling during a celebration.

Arsenal – Raya, White, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Ødegaard, Tzolis, Havertz, Saka

Chelsea – Martinez, Acheampong, Lacroix, Fofana, Neto, James, Lavia, Hato, Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro

title: Burnley announce signing of former Leicester City striker Jamie Vardy
description: Former Leicester City striker Jamie Vardy has joined Burnley on a contract until the end of the season.The 39-year-old arrives at Turf Moor after spending last season in Serie A with Cremonese and wil...
fullText:
Former Leicester City striker Jamie Vardy has joined Burnley on a contract until the end of the season.

The 39-year-old arrives at Turf Moor after spending last season in Serie A with Cremonese and will add significant experience to Nicky Hayen's squad.

"We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley," Hayen said.

"His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign.

"Jamie has a proven track record and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt."

Vardy added: "I'm really happy to now be here at Burnley.

"This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

"I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction."

title: Arsenal could be without four starters in Chelsea clash
description: Arsenal could be without as many as 4 potential starters to face Chelsea today, we’ll soon find out when the teams are out.If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a ...
fullText:
Arsenal could be without as many as 4 potential starters to face Chelsea today, we'll soon find out when the teams are out.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Chelsea and Arsenal face off in the Premier League today in a really exciting game for this stage of the season

So far we've been focused on what's happening in Chelsea's camp – there are fears the Blues are short-handed in midfield after losing Enzo Fernandez on deadline day. But what situation are Arsenal in?

BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND – AUGUST 31: Cristhian Mosquera and Declan Rice of Arsenal applaud the fans before the Premier League 2026/27 match between Aston Villa FC and Arsenal FC at Villa Park on August 31, 2026 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

While Chelsea have an almost fully fit squad, the Gunners have a few more worries. With Willian Saliba out long term, they were hoping to rely on Cristhian Mosquera. However the 22 year old picked up a hamstring injury on Monday night.

Bruno Guimaraes is another doubt – he's missed training this week after also picking up a knock on Monday, but looks like he will be ready to face us today.

Jurrien Timber is another long term absentee. He's close to a return, but a place on the bench looks more likely that a starting spot.

All in all, this is a still a very strong Arsenal team, but there's no doubt they're missing a few important players.

The battle between these two clubs began in the summer, when Morgan Rogers came to Stamford Bridge instead of the Emirates.

title: Ex-Leicester striker Vardy joins Burnley
description: Former Leicester City and England striker Jamie Vardy joins Burnley until the end of the season.
fullText:
Former Leicester City and England striker Jamie Vardy has joined Burnley until the end of the season.

The 39-year-old, who is Leicester's record Premier League scorer with 145 goals, departed for Cremonese in 2025.

Vardy left the Italian side in the summer and now joins the winless Clarets who are bottom of the Championship.

"This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town," Vardy told the club website.

"I can't wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction."

Vardy, who won 26 caps for England, scoring seven goals, spent 13 years at Leicester after signing from non-league Fleetwood Town in 2012.

He went on to score 200 goals in all competitions in 500 appearances.

Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, have made a poor start back in the second tier and have not won in five matches under new boss Nicky Hayen.

On Saturday they conceded two goals in the final 10 minutes to lose 2-1 at home to Bristol City.

"His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign," Hayen added.

"Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt."

title: Clemson Gets Throttled By LSU: 55-10
description: “Best is the Standard” might be a great line, but last night Dabo Swinney showed it is nothing but a line. The only standard the Tigers showed in Baton Rouge was the standard of mediocrity, incompetence, and a return to LSU football from the Tommy Bowden era. This loss was worse than the Orange Bowl, […]
fullText:
"Best is the Standard" might be a great line, but last night Dabo Swinney showed it is nothing but a line. The only standard the Tigers showed in Baton Rouge was the standard of mediocrity, incompetence, and a return to LSU football from the Tommy Bowden era. This loss was worse than the Orange Bowl, worse than 2013 FSU, and worse than losing 5 in a row to the Gamecocks. It was embarrassing, inexcusable, and just plain ugly.

Best case this is a coaching failure for week 1, a few cupcake games followed by an easy schedule in the ACC means the Tigers show improvement over the rest of the season for a 9-3 type season. We may look back at week 1 as an odd game, or just a recognition that the mountain top is further away than we would like, but Clemson is climbing the mountain. But Clemson no longer gets the presumption of competence. Since 2021 the Tigers have shown an inability to compete on the biggest stage without a QB. Big moments are where the Tigers wilt, no longer blessed with 5 star talent, or even 5 heart talent if we are being honest.

It has been 13 years since Clemson has looked this incompetent and defeated from kickoff. We can't even judge the offense because the OL did such a great job of imitating orange traffic cones. The DL looked ok until they were on the field so long that they became traffic cones as well. The same mistakes from the last several years continue to show up. Terrible OL play, a QB that may be ok, but can't function in an environment where they were under pressure from the snap. A DL that isn't creating chaos, LBs that can't run fit to save their lives, and chaos in the secondary. All of these issues are the same things we have talked about for years at this point. It's not worthy of this program and it is not something that should happen when a coach is making 8 figures.

It's Dabo's move now, but based on the evidence over the last 5 seasons it is hard to say anything is going to change. Buckle up everyone.

title: Christian Gonzalez addresses trainer’s contract negotiation comments
description: Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez reacts to the public contract comments made by his trainer on sports radio.
fullText:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. – Christian Gonzalez has stayed fairly quiet regarding his ongoing contract negotiations with the New England Patriots. However, his trainer did quite the opposite.

Christian White recently went on 98.5 The Sports Hub's "Felger and Mazz" to discuss the contract negotiations, saying that while he thought that they were "getting close," the language in the Patriots' offer was "kind of trash."

"It was true at the time, but it's just not all the way true," White said in regard to Kraft's comments about the organization willing to make him the highest-paid cornerback. "Like, the context is like, yeah we did offer you to be the highest paid, but contract language was kind of trash. So, we kind of had to sort through that stuff to make it make sense."

"He's expressed to everybody, he wants to be there," he added. "He's fell in love with the place. He wants to be there for however many more years they agree on the extension, and probably even further after that. I'm just hoping they do right by him."

And with that, White made a bold prediction, saying that he "wouldn't be shocked if this gets done before the Seattle game."

So, what did Gonzalez think of White's comments? Was he upset about his trainer speaking out publicly when he's made a point of keeping it out of the media?

"That's my guy. We have two different opinions," Gonzalez said. "I mean, he's a grown man. If he wants to go talk on the media, he's gonna go talk on the media. He's my guy. I trust him with everything. He trusts me with everything. We talk every day. So it wasn't anything to me that was bad, or I mean, he went and talked to them. So, I talked to him maybe two hours after I came back and saw all that. So I mean, nothing crazy at all.

"We joked about other things, but not about what he said."

title: Valencia manager praises Barcelona ahead of showdown at Mestalla: ‘A team with great potential’
description: Barcelona’s game against Valencia is set to kick off at Mestalla, and Hansi Flick has deployed one of the team’s strongest lineups for the night.With the UEFA Champions League coming up midweek, i...
fullText:
Barcelona's game against Valencia is set to kick off at Mestalla, and Hansi Flick has deployed one of the team's strongest lineups for the night.

With the UEFA Champions League coming up midweek, it is clear that the Barcelona manager wishes to test out his Gala XI in an official game, and the clash against Valencia is that big occasion.

Los Che, meanwhile, have also put up a formidable lineup although they are the underdogs by some distance at their own stadium.

Given the multiple upsets this week in La Liga including Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid losing, however, they will believe they can pull off an upset.

Valencia manager Carlos Corberan faced the media ahead of kickoff and spoke on the game that awaits his side and what he expects from Barcelona on the night.

He was first asked how he planned to stop the Catalans who are the only side yet to drop a point in the league.

"We are well aware of Barcelona's level. It's a team with great potential and many attacking weapons, but our focus is 100% on our team, on what we need to deliver on the pitch, and on how we compete in the match."

Valencia have not enjoyed a great start to the season. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Coming off a rough patch themselves, Valencia enter the game crippled and low on confidence. Corberan then spoke on how he motivated his side ahead of a difficult clash.

"We focus on the things that depend on us: our behavior on the field, our mindset, our desire, our passion, and our intensity."

"These are the things we can control, and that's why we put all our focus on them," he added.

The Valencia manager was then quizzed on Barcelona's midfield and the quality it has with Pedri, Rodri and Fermin Lopez all starting.

"Barcelona has players capable of making a difference in all areas of the pitch," he began, acknowledging the quality all over the field.

"They have speed on the wings, the ability to dominate individual duels, and players who threaten spaces like Raphinha, in addition to midfielders who give them control and the ability to play vertically," he added.

Corberan is aware of Raphinha's threat. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Finally, he spoke out on what his men must do to get at least a point out of the game at Mestalla, saying,

"We must deliver a near-perfect match, with high focus, and play as a single unit, staying close together and constantly helping each other."

"We must also capitalize on the opportunities that come our way, and show character to force Barcelona to defend and not allow them to attack all the time," he concluded.

title: Official: Inter lock Pio Esposito down to new contract until June 2032
description: Inter have officially extended the contract of striker Francesco Pio Esposito to June 2032, locking down the future of the 21-year-old Italy international.The Italian rules had previously limited cont...
fullText:
Inter have officially extended the contract of striker Francesco Pio Esposito to June 2032, locking down the future of the 21-year-old Italy international.

The Italian rules had previously limited contracts to a maximum of five years, but recent changes now allow for six seasons, and this is one of the first real examples of that being used in Serie A.

FLORENCE, ITALY – MARCH 22: Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale celebrates after scoring a goal during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and FC Internazionale at Artemio Franchi on March 22, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images)

The centre-forward has been in their youth academy since 2014, working his way up the levels to become a regular starter alongside captain Lautaro Martinez.

Following a two-season loan spell in Serie B for Spezia, he returned to San Siro in 2025 and flourished under the guidance of coach Cristian Chivu, who had already worked with him in the youth team.

MILAN, ITALY – JANUARY 14: Francesco Pio Esposito of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team's first goal with his Head Coach, Cristian Chivu, during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and US Lecce at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on January 14, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Esposito celebrated his 21st birthday in June and has now scored 12 goals with eight assists in 53 competitive appearances for the senior Inter squad.

He also contributed five goals in just nine senior caps for Italy, making his debut at this level in September 2025.

It is widely reported that the new contract will see his salary improved to €2.7m per season net, compared to the €1.85m he was previously earning.

title: 2. Bundesliga: Osnabrück cruise past Braunschweig with three second-half goals
description: After a goalless first half, Daniel Kofi Kyereh broke the deadlock shortly after the restart before Bjarke Jacobsen and Robin Meißner added further goals to put Osnabrück firmly in control.Yann Stur...
fullText:
After a goalless first half, Daniel Kofi Kyereh broke the deadlock shortly after the restart before Bjarke Jacobsen and Robin Meißner added further goals to put Osnabrück firmly in control.

Yann Sturm scored a late consolation for Braunschweig, but it was not enough to prevent Osnabrück from securing all three points.

The opening stages were relatively cautious, with neither side willing to take too many risks. Osnabrück won the first corner of the afternoon after just five minutes, although the delivery was comfortably dealt with by the Braunschweig defence.

The visitors gradually began to see more of the ball and looked the more threatening side as the first half progressed.

Their best opportunity came in the 21st minute when Andi Hoti struck the post for the visitors, with Osnabrück fortunate not to fall behind.

Braunschweig continued to press for the opener, while Osnabrück struggled to create anything of note in the final third. The hosts did not register their first shot on target until the 41st minute.

Despite Braunschweig's greater attacking threat, neither side could find a breakthrough before half-time, leaving the game goalless at the interval.

Osnabrück head coach Timo Schultz responded by introducing Kyereh at the beginning of the second half, and the substitute immediately made his presence felt.

Just seven minutes after the restart, the hosts took the lead.

Beck delivered a corner into the penalty area, with Jacobsen meeting the cross with a header. Braunschweig goalkeeper Ron-Thorben Hoffmann could only parry the initial effort, leaving Kyereh with the simplest of tasks as he reacted quickest to hammer the rebound into the roof of the net.

Kyereh almost immediately added a second as Osnabrück broke into the Braunschweig penalty area again shortly afterwards, but Hoffmann managed to clear the danger as the visitors survived another scare.

Braunschweig attempted to respond through a series of substitutions, with Junior Zé and Jan Urbich introduced in the 61st minute.

However, Osnabrück continued to look the more dangerous side and eventually doubled their advantage in the 76th minute.

Bjarke Jacobsen found the back of the net to make it 2-0, giving Osnabrück a two-goal cushion and putting the hosts firmly in control.

The result was effectively put beyond doubt just four minutes later when Robin Meißner struck in the 80th minute to make it 3-0.

Braunschweig did manage to find a late consolation through Yann Sturm, who reduced the deficit to 3-1 in the 88th minute.

However, there was to be no late comeback as Osnabrück comfortably saw out the remaining minutes to claim a deserved victory in front of 15,741 supporters at the Bremer Brücke.

title: Netflix Edited WWE Smackdown To Remove A Sex Joke About John Cena
description: This is getting ridiculous.
fullText:
When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

The conversation around Netflix's censorship of WWE content has gotten particularly loud recently, and this latest example of sanitizing certainly isn't going to quiet the frustration. For the second time in a month, the streaming service changed the edit to completely remove a reference a wrestler made to another's sexual past. This time, the joke involved John Cena and was particularly noticeable because USA Network aired the segment unedited at the same time.

The specifics of WWE broadcasting can be a little complicated; so, let me explain how exactly it all works. Monday Night Raw streams on Netflix for basically everyone, regardless of where they live. Friday Night Smackdown streams on Netflix for most of the world but airs on USA Network in the United States. Because wrestling fans post clips from WWE programming all the time, it's really easy to tell when something was changed, and lately, there have been a lot of changes.

Last night is a perfect example. In the version I watched in the United States, Nikki Bella and Paige got into a scripted argument backstage. Bella seemingly referenced explicit sexual materials that were stolen off Paige's phone and leaked some years ago by saying we all know she has "more passion" behind closed doors. Paige fired back and said she built her career on Hustle, Loyalty and Respect, while Nikki just slept with it. That's, of course, a reference to John Cena's longtime catchphrase and a sick burn since Bella was previously engaged to Cena.

Unfortunately, that sick burn was nowhere to be found in Netflix's version. The streamer kept in Paige's reference to Hustle, Loyalty and Respect but removed the part where she said you just slept with it. Instead, the segment cut to the crowd and then cut back after the line was delivered, leaving everyone watching internationally unaware of what was actually said.

You can check out this side-by-side of the two versions that wrestling fans are passing around Twitter…

USA Network LIVE Version - Paige to Nikki Bella: “I built my career on hustle, loyalty & respect and you just slept with it.”Netflix REPLAY Version - Cuts the slept line*COME ON MAN TF LMAO 😭 pic.twitter.com/m9OkVslJyV

— @CeaserWrestles (September 5, 2026)

The specifics of what happened here are quite similar to a separate censorship decision that happened in early August. In that instance, Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan were in an argument, and Lynch fired off a series of insults. She said Becky wasn't the best WWE Champion in her own stable (a reference to Raquel Rodriguez) and then said she wasn't even the best WWE Champion that slept with Dominik Mysterio (a reference to Rhea Ripley). The line went over huge with the in-person crowd and viewers watching the show live, but by the next morning, Netflix had gone back and re-cut the episode to replace the Dominik Mysterio joke with footage of the crowd.

It's not just PG-level sex jokes that Netflix seems to have a problem with either. On the last episode of Monday Night Raw, the streamer heavily edited multiple segments of the show to pixelate the faces of a few wrestlers who were bleeding. The footage looked almost comical with all the blurring. It also reportedly caused so much frustration within WWE that the company released an uncensored version on social media because once again, the version that aired looked so stupid.

I watched wrestling as a child and am supportive of WWE and Netflix keeping the show family-friendly, but the line over the past month or so has gotten absolutely ridiculous. Entertainment for all ages means you're going to get the occasional non-graphic reference to sex, and it means you're sometimes going to see a little blood. That's just a representation of real life, and ten year olds can handle that level of adult entertainment.

Whether everyone got to see the line or not, I'm excited for Nikki and Paige's feud. The two are good friends in real life, and judging by the fact that they decided to tap into each other's pasts, they're very willing to go there to sell the storyline. I can't wait to see how the rest of this plays out. It should be a ton of fun, at least provided we get to actually see all the best zingers.

title: What Lane Kiffin said about being hated after LSU’s 51-10 win over Clemson
description: LSU spent the week before its opener in a Louisiana courtroom and in an exchange of statements with the SEC over the eligibility of former NFL players on college rosters. Lane Kiffin’s first team then beat Clemson 51-10 in Baton Rouge on Saturday night, and he brought the argument up himself at halftime. With LSU […] The post What Lane Kiffin said about being hated after LSU’s 51-10 win over Clemson appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
LSU spent the week before its opener in a Louisiana courtroom and in an exchange of statements with the SEC over the eligibility of former NFL players on college rosters. Lane Kiffin's first team then beat Clemson 51-10 in Baton Rouge on Saturday night, and he brought the argument up himself at halftime.

With LSU ahead 31-3 and holding a 336-54 edge in total yards at the break, Kiffin finished his interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe, started to walk away, then came back to the microphone and said, "Imagine if we had pro players."

Two days earlier, East Baton Rouge Parish Judge William Jorden granted a preliminary injunction barring the NCAA and the SEC from punishing schools that rostered any of the 42 athletes suing for a fifth season of eligibility, which cleared former Ole Miss players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to follow Kiffin to Baton Rouge. The SEC filed its own federal lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin in Alabama that same morning. LSU submitted a 103-man roster on Friday and left the two spots empty.

Kiffin explained that decision on ESPN's "College GameDay" hours before kickoff.

"That wasn't easy, as much as I feel for the players," he said. "And I believe that you fight for what you believe in. And I believe these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters. But at the same time, I'm the head coach of LSU, and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster."

"I'm just really glad they played the way they did, so that wouldn't have been the story, because I get it, it would have been the whole story," Kiffin said after the game. "Even if we won close, kind of ugly, the whole story would have been, man, I screwed the team up by doing this. I said it this morning, you can not agree with it. I've been criticized heavily for the last two weeks, and I get that."

Kiffin said someone asked him afterward if he had really put the halftime line on the air.

"What's the difference?" he answered. "Everybody hates you. They can't hate you much more."

Lane Kiffin, when asked about his halftime comments of “imagine if we had pro players”

Says someone asked him if he really said that..

Kiffin: “What’s the difference? Everybody hates you. They can’t hate you much more” pic.twitter.com/m4OwIOaxHI

— Trey Wallace (@TreyWallace) September 6, 2026

“Imagine if we had pro players.”

Lane Kiffin is not holding back. pic.twitter.com/OzHEZqw1UW

— ESPN (@espn) September 6, 2026

LSU ran for 213 yards before halftime against a Clemson team that finished the two quarters with minus-4 on the ground, and that gap is why the joke played as a joke. The 41-point margin was the worst loss of Dabo Swinney's tenure at Clemson and the program's worst since 2000.

Kiffin also pushed back on the idea that the week's noise reached his players, calling that talk overrated. The two roster spots remain open, and the SEC's federal case remains pending.

The post What Lane Kiffin said about being hated after LSU's 51-10 win over Clemson appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.

title: Steelers have a hidden advantage in Joey Porter Jr. contract talks
description: The Pittsburgh Steelers
fullText:
It's no secret that the Pittsburgh Steelers find themselves between a rock and a hard place when it comes to contract negotiations with Joey Porter Jr.

The team recently handed out multiple extensions and finds itself a little strapped for cap space, while Porter is reportedly considering drastic measures in pursuit of a new deal. But the team holds an ace up its sleeve if the contract talks reach a point of no return: the franchise tag.

Porter's rookie contract is set to expire following the 2026 season, and the Steelers have historically not negotiated new deals mid-season. This means Pittsburgh has a week to sign Porter to a huge, potentially $30-million-plus deal before September 13. That seems unlikely given the noise surrounding the two sides.

The Steelers, however, can franchise tag Porter following this season, which would cost around $23 million. This would either allow the team to continue negotiating during the 2027 offseason or attempt to at least pick up some trade capital for the talented Porter.

This situation has blown up in the Steelers' face before, such as the Le'Veon Bell holdout. But there are very few choices the team has left if both sides can't come to an agreement this week.

title: Tennessee-Furman ties second-highest temperature at Neyland Stadium
description: Neyland Stadium has second-highest temperature football game all time in recorded history.
fullText:
Tennessee's football game against Furman on Sept. 5 tied the second-highest kickoff temperature at Neyland Stadium in recorded history (1950-present), according to the University of Tennessee.

The Vols', 56-9, season-opening victory was the fifth game at Neyland Stadium with a kickoff temperature at or above 90 degrees.

The highest kickoff temperature at Neyland Stadium was 91 degrees versus Florida on Sept. 24, 2016.

Other football games with 90-degree temperatures were against ETSU on Sept. 8, 2018, Southern Miss on Sept. 8, 2007 and Wyoming on Sept. 4, 1999.

101,915 were in attendance for the Tennessee-Furman game, marking a 28th consecutive sellout at Neyland Stadium and a streak that dates to Sept. 17, 2022.

Tennessee's 2026 season opener kicked off at 3:32 p.m. EDT and concluded at 6:53 p.m. EDT.

The Vols have a 98-26-6 on-field record all time in season openers, including a 6-0 record under head coach Josh Heupel since his first season in 2021.

title: How integral to Bills defense line will Greg Gaines be in 2026?
description: Buffalo had been linked to a nose tackle from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but they acquired his former teammate instead
fullText:
With a switch to an odd-man front on defense, the Buffalo Bills have been changing their defensive personnel throughout this offseason. In some ways, the team has had to be creative, asking players drafted for former head coach Sean McDermott's four-man defensive line to change their roles and body types in preparation for a season under new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. In some cases, though, the Bills have gone outside of their usual comfort areas to find different player archetypes.

One of the more oft-discussed positions in the new defense has been that of the nose tackle. Buffalo didn't have a traditional nose tackle with McDermott given that they generally had two defensive tackles on the field at once, but players like DaQuan Jones and Star Lotulelei served roles similar to that which a nose tackle would traditionally fill in a three-man front. The Bills have an answer in the middle, but they definitely need depth at that spot.

In today's installment of our "91 players in 91 days" series, we discuss a veteran nose tackle ostensibly signed to provide said depth.
_____________________________________________________________________________

Experience/Draft:  7; selected by the Los Angeles Rams in the fourth round (No. 134 overall) of the 2019 NFL Draft

Acquired:  Signed with Buffalo on 8/18/2026

Financial situation (per Spotrac):  Gaines signed a one-year deal at the veteran's minimum. The total deal is worth $1,487,500, but thanks to the veteran's salary benefit, his cap hit comes in lower at $1,262,500 for the season. If Gaines is on Buffalo's Week One roster, his entire base salary ($1.3 million) becomes guaranteed thanks to his status as a fully vested veteran. If he's released prior to the start of the first game, Buffalo will carry a dead cap charge of $137,500 for the season.

2025 Recap:  Gaines once again served as a rotational nose tackle for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last season, appearing on 35% of the team's defensive snaps across 17 games. Gaines offers little in the way of pass rush, so he mostly plays on early downs and in obvious run situations, acting as a gap-plugger and run-stuffer up front. He totaled 23 tackles, three tackles for loss, and two sacks last season.

Positional outlook:  Gaines is one of ten defensive linemen listed on the current roster. Ed Oliver, Deone Walker, Landon Jackson, Zane Durant, Phidarian Mathis, Zion Logue, DeWayne Carter, Travis Clayton, and T.J. Sanders are the others.

2026 Offseason:  Gaines has been a free agent since his contract with Tampa Bay expired at the start of the new league year. He has participated in practice and preseason action since signing with Buffalo.

2026 Season outlook: While he fills a need as a potential nose tackle, as Skarekrow pointed out in his All-22 analysis after Gaines signed, the veteran can play multiple spots along a three-man line. Tampa Bay frequently used him off center, and while that might have been because they had Vita Vea to plug the middle, it bodes well for Gaines' chances to come in and contribute along the line in Buffalo.

Behind Deone Walker, Buffalo doesn't have much going at nose tackle. Phidarian Mathis looked like a solid bet to make the team as the backup nose, but a three-game suspension for an alcohol-use issue while he was with the New York Jets means that he will begin the year unavailable. I guess being with the Jets could drive anyone to drink, but I digress. The Bills have also asked third-year man DeWayne Carter to bulk up and play the nose, and while he has done so, he hasn't exactly separated himself this summer, and after a weak rookie season followed by a lost second year due to a torn Achilles, it's not wise to assume that he can just come in and play at the level Buffalo needs.

Gaines, then, not only has a good shot at making the roster based on his experience alone, but I would go so far as to say he has a strong chance to carve out an important role on defense. Whether he's spelling Walker or playing alongside him on first down, in goal line situations, or on fourth-and-short, Gaines could easily see 35-45% of the snaps on defense as a run-down specialist. The Bills don't have a ton of those along their defensive front, and given Leonhard's stated desire to be significantly better against the run this season, it's reasonable to assume that someone like Gaines is looked at as an acquisition who can help them in achieving that goal.

August signings are often nothing more than camp bodies and tryout players, but with Greg Gaines, the Bills likely found a piece to their defense that they were missing.

title: Liverpool FC’s New Speed Merchants Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz
description: Pace might not be everything but it sure feels good to know Liverpool’s squad now has it back.
fullText:
When new head coach Andoni Iraola was announced it was soon clear that an essential part of his style demanded pacy wingers which was music to the ears of Reds supporters because we had just survived one of the slowest approaches to play in the previous season.

There was a time not too far back where Liverpool boasted one of the greatest ever attacking units in football of Mohamed Salah, Sadio Mane and Roberto Firmino. All three complimented each other with Firmino the purely selfless one who took joy in setting up Mo and Mane with some outrageous flicks and tricks plus the uncanny way of knowing exactly where the other two would be without needing to look. Something else though was the shear power and pace that sucked the air out of opponents who were left wondering how their attack was suddenly turned into a goal down the other end of the pitch for Liverpool.

Coming back to the present and even though it's early days there is no denying that the Reds have pace to burn down the wings with new signings Barcola and Munoz. Of course there is more to just running fast but it seems that both have skills to match and the lesser known Munoz already has an assist via being fouled in the penalty box after bursting into it with the ball as well a goal that earned us a point against Nottingham Forest. Is Munoz raw? yes he is but it's a natural pace and determined energy which saw him selected for the 2026 World Cup winning Spanish national squad.

This writer is reminded of former Red Xherdan Shaqiri when watching Munoz and most of that is down to physical build as well power which isn't to say there is a lack of footballing skill, far from it, but the physical impact is impossible to ignore. It's also very impressive how Munoz, who has predominately played on the left, is having such an impact on the right that he is the obvious starter and for this writer it's quelled the frustration that a right winger wasn't brought during the summer. To be honest the fixation on that factor is not something that concerns Iraola and both Munoz's performances and Iraola demand for positional flexibility is refreshing and proof that such rigid structuring of roles can be unnecessarily restricting.

On Friday night in the game against Ipswich our new signing Bradley Barcola made his debut for the last thirty minutes and the traveling Reds sang his song (originally former Maxi Rodriguez's song) as he stepped onto the pitch. As much as the supporters would have loved to see Barcola score or get an assist that wasn't the expectation but he did break a 26/27 Premier League season record (early days yes) for top speed by a player with one run reaching 35.9km/h (according to FotMob).

Barcola's recent career performances with PSG and also being a member of the French national squad means we already know he is an elite player with a lot of experience yet it still came as a surprise, to this writer at least, that in Barcola's first appearance for Liverpool he would be getting up to those kind of speeds.

Possibly the one thought of caution in some supporter's heads is that teams setting up low-blocks will make pace something of little value and that does seem to hold water yet there is no hiding from the fact that Liverpool really suffered with no pace last season. It's also better to have tools that are ready to be used at any given moment than not have those particular tools available and both Munoz and Barcola have much more to offer than pace alone.

With the first 26/27 Champions league game at Anfield on Wednesday night it will be exciting to witness Liverpool's new speed merchants racing down the wingers, one with a little more grace while the other will power through all opponents without fear.

title: Why Matt Campbell says his Penn State coaching debut was special
description: Matt Campbell took a few moments to soak in the reality of making his head coaching debut at Penn State but quickly shifted his focus on the game.
fullText:
Matt Campbell made some history in his head coaching debut on Saturday, but his focus was all on doing whatever it takes for his program to record a win. Maybe Campbell took a few minutes to soak everything in as he made his head coaching debut with Penn State in a packed Beaver Stadium, but he did not seem to let that get in the way of the job at hand.

"It was really special to be a part of this for the first time, and you know so many people say how special it is to play football here, but it was really special to coach here today," Campbell said in his postgame press conference following Penn State's 45-0 victory over Marshall. "The environment was second to none."

As far as reflecting on the moment for Campbell, that was about as much as he was willing to dish to the media before shifting his focus on to the success of the team on the field.

"I know everybody's looking for that magic answer, and I hate to tell you this, that was awesome early, but now you're responsible for the game and for me, this team, and earning the right to at least get to a game," Campbell continued to say in his postgame press conference. "I  was so anxious of watching who this football team could be, and where we could respond, and obviously we know just a little bit, but we got great videotape evidence now in a chaotic game environment."

Campbell explained that he let one of his staff members, Jordan Hill, help take the charge in getting his team ready to play in front of the Beaver Stadium environment in a real game. With so many transfers and new faces on the roster, it helped for Campbell to have a former Nittany Lion who understands this place to deliver that message throughout the week.

"Jordan Hill leads, he works with our leadership group, with myself and Jordan, and I thought he did a great job on Monday talking to our players about this is a special place to play football, and it means something to this crowd and this fanbase," Campbell said in his postgame press conference."

"To want to come out and watch our fans and watch what this place feels like and maybe look up and you see those teams on the scoreboard or on our press box and what it's meant to our great coaches and players to play here," Campbell said. "You're just grateful to have the opportunity as a football team to continue to try to represent the past of this program."

Campbell will now get a chance to see what it is like to coach Penn State on the road in Week 2. Penn State travels to Philadelphia to take on Temple. Lincoln Financial Field will likely be a bit like a home-away-from-home environment, with Penn State fans helping to pack Temple's home stadium on Saturday, Sept. 12.

title: Division III power Mount Union loses in Week 1 to snap 85-game regular-season win streak that dated back to 2016
description: The loss was also Mount Union's first Week 1 loss since 1987.
fullText:
Division III powerhouse Mount Union lost its first regular-season game since 2016 on Saturday.

The Purple Raiders fell 24-23 to Wheaton in their 2026 season-opener after Wheaton blocked a game-tying extra point with 22 seconds to go. Mount Union's Kayden Minner scored on a 1-yard run ahead of the failed extra point, and the Purple Raiders elected to go for the tie and potential overtime instead of what could have been a game-winning two-point conversion.

After blocking the PAT, Wheaton then recovered Mount Union's onside kick.

The loss snapped a regular-season win streak that lasted 85 games. Before Saturday, the last time Mount Union lost a non-playoff game was on Nov. 12, 2016, when John Carroll scored a 31-28 win. Most of the members of that Mount Union team are now in their 30s.

Mount Union made the semifinals of the D3 playoffs that season and won the 2017 national title with a 15-0 season. Since then, the team has, remarkably, not won a national championship as the regular-season win streak lived on. Over the past six full seasons, Mount Union has lost the Stagg Bowl three times and was eliminated in the third round of the Division III playoffs in 2025 after an 11-0 start.

Saturday's loss was also the first time Mount Union had lost a Week 1 game in 39 years. Until 2026, the team's most recent season-opening loss came in a 17-15 defeat to Wooster in 1987.
