title: Badiashile suffers nightmare Napoli debut as Chelsea loanee slammed: ‘His fault’
description: Chelsea loanee Benoît Badiashile received low ratings from Italian sports papers following Napoli’s 3-2 loss against Inter, with the French centre-back blamed for two of the Nerazzurri’s goals.N...
fullText:
Chelsea loanee Benoît Badiashile received low ratings from Italian sports papers following Napoli's 3-2 loss against Inter, with the French centre-back blamed for two of the Nerazzurri's goals.

Napoli wasted a two-goal lead in their away game against Inter on Saturday, suffering their second consecutive loss in Serie A.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Marcus Thuram of Internazionale celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Chelsea loanee Badiashile made his Serie A debut coming off the bench in the final ten minutes, with the Partenopei leading 2-1, but his impact was beyond negative.

Inter striker Thuram overjumped him to score Inter's equaliser, but the Napoli defender was also blamed for the Nerazzurri's winner, scored by Lautaro Martinez in stoppage time.

Football Italia rated Badiashile 5/10, the same mark he received from Gazzetta dello Sport and Tuttosport.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 05: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of Napoli, reacts during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and SSC Napoli at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 05, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Gazzetta blamed Badiashile for Inter's second goal, but also criticised Massimiliano Allegri for introducing the Chelsea loanee: "Badiashile lost Thuram, who headed home the equaliser," the pink paper wrote.

"It was his fault, but also the fault of whoever decided to bring on a new defender who hadn't played in ages at the most crucial moment."

Corriere dello Sport was even harsher on Badiashile, rating him 4.5/10: "He hadn't played since March 7, and he showed. Thuram outjumped him for the header, and he was also partly at fault for the third goal."

LONDON, ENGLAND – JANUARY 31: Benoit Badiashile of Chelsea reacts during the Premier League match between Chelsea and West Ham United at Stamford Bridge on January 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Badiashile joined Napoli on a paid €3m loan deal from Chelsea this summer. The Partenopei have an option to make his move permanent for €27m at the end of the season.

Napoli's next game is against Arsenal at the Stadio Maradona next Wednesday, in their 2026-27 Champions League opener.

title: Blades owners speak - but many questions remain
description: BBC Radio Sheffield's Rob Staton reflects on a podcast appearance by Sheffield United owner Steve Rosen - but says questions remain unanswered.
fullText:
"Steve, we've known each other a long time."

And there begins the first long-form interview by anyone involved in Sheffield United's current ownership.

Nathan Zegura, a summariser known as 'the voice' of the Cleveland Browns, is the man sat across from Steve Rosen, the co-chairman at Bramall Lane. They appear to be friends.

It's the kind of conversation that would have been really welcome at the start of Rosen's tenure at United. A warm 'get to know you' piece.

It's not appropriate now though, 18 months into what has been a chaotic period of ownership.

They gave manager Chris Wilder a new contract in January 2025, only to part ways months later.

They then had to go cap in hand back to Wilder after his replacement Ruben Selles lost every game in a disastrous short spell in charge.

This all came after working with pro-gambler James Bord as an advisor, who months later would fail in a bid to buy city rivals Sheffield Wednesday, after squandering money on a list of bad signings.

Maybe things would settle down after that? Nope.

This summer we've had the former owners, United World, claiming they're owed £35m as part of the sale.

This has never been disputed. The holding company that originally controlled United has been liquidated.

Questions remain how the current owners intend to handle the situation, and what actions the English Football League (EFL) and Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will take, if any, following a truly bizarre set of circumstances.

None of these matters are properly addressed in this long-awaited interview. They are airily discussed as if it's merely part of the rough and tumble of running a club.

Every statement on the United World situation and the threat of a possible points deduction has been dismissive, more or less saying it's a storm in a tea cup. There was more of that here.

This is the exchange between Rosen and Negura on the matter:

Rosen: "I can't see in any scenario where the club gets a points deduction because of the (EFL's) insolvency rule. It wasn't like Sheffield Wednesday where they had an administrator and it went into insolvency, couldn't pay their bills and all that. That's not our situation."

Rosen: "Yeah, really good, right?"

Negura: "Because all this is all about winning. Yeah?"

Rosen: "(It's) all about winning."

This isn't an adequate addressing of a significant worry for many fans. We simply don't know yet what the EFL or IFR will do, either, irrespective of what's said here.

To be fair, others have welcomed the opportunity to hear from Rosen. They've even suggested he comes across well. I don't disagree. He's a good talker. He's definitely not an uninteresting person.

But now is not the time to gloss over the big issues off the pitch. It isn't the time to speak about a desire to create United's version of the 'Dawg Pound' - a section of the Cleveland Browns' stadium where fans dress up in costumes and paint their faces.

The last thing we need at Bramall Lane is the Kop turning into a Jack Sparrow convention in honour of Captain Blade.

Neither did it feel appropriate to ask for an explanation on what relegation is. Die-hard Blades have waited ages to hear from the men at the top of their club and when they finally get something, this is what they're subjected to?

The whole thing felt like a safe means to end accusations that the owners never speak - but does this really count? A podcast chat with a mate, skirting around the big issues with a smile?

There are still serious questions to be asked and clarity to be delivered. Neither Rosen nor his co-chairman Helmy Eltoukhy have spoken to the Sheffield media since buying the club.

The invitation is still very much open. The fans deserve it, because we'll be willing to ask the questions that need to be asked. The owners should also be expected to come up with convincing answers under pressure.

title: What Was Reggie Barlow Thinking?
description: We’ve all seen it. A college football game is coming to its inevitable end. And as is so often the case, there’s going to be a winner, there’s going to be a loser, and everyone watching knows who the latter will be. The cameras pan to the coach of the soon to be losing team. […]
fullText:
We've all seen it. A college football game is coming to its inevitable end. And as is so often the case, there's going to be a winner, there's going to be a loser, and everyone watching knows who the latter will be. The cameras pan to the coach of the soon to be losing team. He stares into the middle distance, contemplating decisions made and actions taken, questioning his strategy, his tactics, and his very worth as a coach of football and a leader of young men.

"Lou Holtz's chartreuse Maserati!" you exclaim. "What must that poor sap be thinking right now?"

Ladies and gentlemen, this is Tennessee State head coach Reggie Barlow gamely facing the media following his team's 63-3 loss to Georgia.

I ask you: what was Reggie Barlow thinking?

a) "Look, they were going to beat the ever-loving stew out of somebody in week one. Might as well be us."

b) "Wait, they really gained 611 yards of offense? I saw that on the stat sheet and just assumed I was hallucinating from the heat."

c) "Hey, we decided to start the season against a truly elite national program. But only because Clemson was already spoken for."

d) "I feel bad that I shrieked and jumped under the desk when the guy from the Bogart Biweekly called my name. But he looked a little like Raylen Wilson and I didn't want to take any chances."

Feel free to offer your own suggestions in the comments below. And… Feel free to offer your own suggestions in the comments below. And…

title: Kleindienst takes aim at Gladbach teammates after collapse against Elversberg
description: Borussia Mönchengladbach have endured a miserable start to the Bundesliga season, picking up zero points from their opening two games.After being beaten 3-0 by RB Leipzig in their opener, Die Fohlen ...
fullText:
Borussia Mönchengladbach have endured a miserable start to the Bundesliga season, picking up zero points from their opening two games.

After being beaten 3-0 by RB Leipzig in their opener, Die Fohlen looked on course for their first win when they raced into a 3-1 lead against SV Elversberg at Borussia-Park on Saturday.

However, they completely let the game slip away, eventually suffering a dramatic 4-3 defeat.

Speaking to ZDF after the game, Gladbach captain Tim Kleindienst was furious with the mistakes and lapses in concentration that allowed Elversberg back into the match.

"We need to raise our level of focus as quickly as possible so that it lasts for 90 minutes. And I have no idea what the reason is – maybe watch less TikTok or whatever. I honestly don't care what they do," Kleindienst said, delivering a blunt message to his teammates.

"At the end of the day, they just need to do something so that they stay clear-headed for 90 minutes, make it through the full 90 minutes, and keep their focus so that we can defend until the very end. And not keep giving the ball away needlessly, making misplaced passes and committing fouls."

title: “Outrageous and Indefensible”: Skip Bayless Fumes as Michigan Secure Hail Mary Win Over Western Michigan
description: The Michigan Wolverines’ season opener against the Western Michigan Broncos ended in the most dramatic way possible. Western Michigan looked to have sealed a remarkable upset when Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood’s Hail Mary attempt landed out of bounds as time expired.
fullText:
The Michigan Wolverines' season opener against the Western Michigan Broncos ended in the most dramatic way possible.

Western Michigan looked to have sealed a remarkable upset when Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt landed out of bounds as time expired. However, despite TV replays showing that the clock had hit zero before the ball hit a Western Michigan defender, officials put a second back on the clock, giving the Wolverines one more play. This time, Underwood connected with wide receiver JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard score, sealing a controversial win.

Sports analyst Skip Bayless said it was unfair that the Wolverines were awarded one more play to score.

"Giving Michigan one more play just might've been the most outrageous and indefensible home cooking I've ever witnessed," Bayless wrote.

Underwood led the charge with a touchdown and 170 passing yards as Michigan chalked up its first win of the year in dramatic fashion.

Even though Skip Bayless called out the manner of the Michigan Wolverines' victory, he was still glad about the result. In another post on X/Twitter, Bayless said that as an Oklahoma Sooners fan, he'd rather they face the Wolverines after a win than a loss.

"As an Oklahoma fan, I'm glad Michigan managed to pull out its first game under Kyle Whittingham. Would not have wanted my Sooners going up to Ann Arbor next Saturday with the Wolverines seething after a home loss to Western Michigan," Bayless shared.

Brent Venables' Sooners are scheduled to face Kyle Whittingham's Wolverines on Saturday, Sept. 12.

title: How McLaren left itself exposed at the F1 Italian Grand Prix
description: McLaren's qualifying slip-ups at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix masked encouraging performance on what was supposed to be a tough track for the team
fullText:
As Pierre Gasly and Alpine mastered the qualifying game to perfection at Monza, McLaren was one of several Formula 1 teams wondering what could have been after several key factors led to an underwhelming Italian Grand Prix qualifying result.

Off the back of two wins at high downforce circuits in Budapest and Zandvoort, high-speed Monza was never expected to be McLaren's strongest track, both because of a slightly less aero efficient car and a known weakness in low-speed chicanes.

In fact, team principal Andrea Stella called the Temple of Speed a good test to see if McLaren's progress was able to carry over on different track layouts. Looking at Q2, the MCL40 looked set to pass that test with flying colours, with Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris second and third behind Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli.

But, like several other frontrunners, McLaren couldn't replicate that form in Q3. Piastri only found a tenth on his first Q3 run, while Norris was exposed by Piastri's off at Turn 1, robbing him of a crucial slipstream from his team-mate.

As Gasly's shock pole in the Alpine showed, execution was everything, ranging from battery and tyre management to on-track positioning on the outlap to find the perfect tow. That's where Mercedes' George Russell lost pole as he was too close behind a cunning Max Verstappen and, according to Stella, his team's Q3 execution also cost it a better result than third for Piastri and a lowly ninth for Norris.

"When we executed well, like in Q2, we had the two cars P1, P2, then they ended up P2, P3 at the end of Q2, because the cars were positioned in the right place in terms of slipstream, and both Oscar and Lando drove the cars very well despite the small gaps to the cars ahead," Stella explained.

"[In Q3] on the first attempt probably Lando had too big a gap to the car ahead, he lost some time in some corners. So, in terms of execution we leave some performance behind, while Oscar did a very good lap. Then, in the final run, we had some issues managing the battery, and here in Monza every percent of battery charge costs you a significant amount of milliseconds. And then we had the issue with Oscar locking in corner 1. So overall, there are multiple areas in which we have not executed at the level that we should have."

One mitigating factor, though Stella was keen not to call it in as an excuse, was McLaren's garage position at the end of the pitlane. That heavily encouraged the McLarens to go out first for the final run, because if they had waited for others they were at risk of getting blocked leaving their pit box by a train of cars in the fast lane. That would relegate them to the tail end of the field, with a chance of not being able to start the final attempt before the clock runs out.

As it was, Piastri and Norris were first in the train with no other cars to collect a slipstream from ahead of them. With the Australian then missing his braking point into Turn 1, it left Norris all exposed.

"At no point should this be an excuse, but when you are at the first garage, you need to be a little bit careful in leaving the garage too late, because if you are the last one, there's a risk that then you're not going to be in time opening the lap," Stella explained. "So that's also why we found ourselves being first, but probably we have to review the margins that we adopted, because then being first with the slipstream effect that we have this year seems definitely a position that you don't want to be."

Piastri's lock-up in Turn 1, hurting his team-mate in the process, sent the internet's conspiracy theorists into a frenzy, though both he and Norris had been struggling with front-tyre locking into the chicane all day. F1's 2026 battery management needs on energy-starved Monza made it tough for drivers to work heat into their brakes, Stella explained, because they couldn't afford to deviate from their optimal energy harvesting strategy.

"It's very specific to Monza," the Italian said. "There's not much energy that you can spend in an outlap to properly work your brakes, because the harvest is so limited that you need to pay a lot of attention to it. It's not like you can do lots of acceleration and braking, warm up your brakes, plus if you start to do so, you may lose contact with the car ahead, so it's very tricky.

"That's certainly something that we might have to look into in terms of making sure that the brakes can operate even without this input of energy that you have to give in outlaps, but I would say that the problem here is very much Monza-specific."

Overall, Stella felt the team's underlying performance was encouraging for other low-draw circuits on the calendar and said its lack of aero efficiency was a "red herring" given the improvements the team had made to the car, including the introduction of its rotating rear wing design.

If Monza was an exam for the overall performance of the MCL40, Stella gave his team a half pass. "Our engineers have done a good job of minimising drag, and once we also optimised the power unit and the energy management, we were actually not that far off in terms of top speed. It would be a little bit of a red herring or an excuse to say we have too much drag.

"I think if we had done a better job of execution and controlling some parameters that don't only depend on the pure performance of the car, we could have definitely qualified on the first couple of rows on the grid. So, it's almost a half pass from a performance point of view in terms of Monza being an exam."

title: Ira Winderman: Heat at top of East or play-in? It’s a very fine line.
description: MIAMI — The prevailing notion once LeBron James put pen to paper on July 27 was that the stage was set in the Eastern Conference, that assessments could be set when it came to standings, seedings. Yes, there was some cleanup work around the conference in the interim, most notably the Cavaliers’ acquisition of Peyton Watson, but otherwise mostly ancillary stuff, like the 76ers adding Kentavious ...
fullText:
MIAMI — The prevailing notion once LeBron James put pen to paper on July 27 was that the stage was set in the Eastern Conference, that assessments could be set when it came to standings, seedings.

Yes, there was some cleanup work around the conference in the interim, most notably the Cavaliers' acquisition of Peyton Watson, but otherwise mostly ancillary stuff, like the 76ers adding Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Charlotte adding Dennis Schroder, and the Heat signing Klay Thompson and Nick Richards.

And then came Kawhi Day on Wednesday, in all its NBA drama in regard to the death penalties delivered to the Los Angeles Clippers.

Because with that finality, it meant that Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors again was a thing, an East acquisition on a level somewhere between Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Heat and Jaylen Brown to the 76ers.

So, no, we weren't done with the LeBron-a-thon resetting the East.

But now we seemingly should be.

Because the Raptors are for real, perhaps as for real as when Leonard last was in the team's colors, during that run to the 2019 title.

So now, and only now, can stock truly be taken of where Pat Riley's massive Miami makeover has left the Heat in a conference upgraded with significant talent, what with both LeBron and Kawhi coming East.

At the moment, FanDuel lists 10 Eastern Conference teams with projected winning records, which also is the limit for postseason spots (when counting the four play-in seeds).

From that list, FanDuel has the Heat tied with the Raptors for the sixth and final direct entry to the playoffs, as the No. 6 seed, at 45 1/2 wins.

So Heat play-in for a fifth consecutive season?

Or ready to challenge not only for direct entry into the playoffs, but potentially even homecourt in the first round?

But at least now, with Kawhi resolution, cases can be made in earnest.

Considering the Pistons won the East last season at 60-22, projecting the conference's best at 52 1/2 wins speaks volumes about the competition in the East.

Last season's championship had a lightning-in-a-bottle feel, with New York City seemingly celebrating as such.

Subbing in Andre Drummond for Mitchell Robinson is a downgrade, which could lead to a downturn from the Knicks' 53 victories last season.

This is not like chasing the Thunder at the top of the West.

The top seed in the East is there for the taking.

In light of the Jaylen Brown trade, it's almost as if the Celtics are being viewed as top two in the East based on reputation.

For all the power tandems in the East, who exactly stands as second-best Celtic to Jayson Tatum? Derrick White? Paul George?

And for all the doubts about the Heat's depth, it's not exactly as if the Celtics are rolling out starting-level talent off their bench, with all due respect to Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez and Baylor Scheierman.

Tobias Harris out and John Collins in. Is that necessarily an upgrade? And don't discount the loss of Isaiah Stewart and his incredible bulk.

Yes, there were gains in the margins with the additions of Isaiah Joe, Gary Harris and Taurean Prince, but there remains the question of one-year wonder or something more from the Pistons.

The addition of Peyton Watson is meaningful, but consider also how it came at the cost of Max Strus, Dean Wade and Dennis Schroder.

After consecutive playoff flameouts, is the motivation still there?

Any time a team puts this much stock into James Harden, doubts are reasonable.

Is it fantasy (as in stats) or reality when it comes to this much talent in a single lineup?

The usage rate with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Anfernee Simons and VJ Edgecombe seemingly would require at least 1 1/2 balls in play to sate all six based on last season's numbers.

Something has to give. The talent is there, but it is a huge sum of a lot of parts for Nick Nurse to manage.

When it comes to measuring up to the Heat, you could start here: Which duo is better – Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo for the Heat or Leonard and Scottie Barnes for the Raptors? Taking either side would be by the slimmest of margins.

Then, looking at the remainder of the Raptors' roster, a case that with the likes of RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, Ja'Kobe Walter, Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Broyles, there is depth that measures up to the Heat.

The games between the teams have always been close … so could this season's final record.

As mentioned above with the example with the Raptors, where does Antetokounmpo-Adebayo stand in the East? On par with Toronto's Leonard-Barnes, the Knicks' Jalen Brunson-Karl-Anthony Towns, the Celtics' Tatum-White, the Pistons' Cade Cunningham-Jalen Duren, the Cavaliers' Donovan Mitchell-Harden, or any 76ers two-man group?

Otherwise, the Heat's supporting case seemingly is being sold short by most, when considering the presence of Andrew Wiggins, Davion Mitchell, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Klay Thompson and Pelle Larsson, to name a half-dozen supporting players.

Did we mention that Tyrese Haliburton is back? Or that Ivica Zubac is about to start his first full season with the Pacers?

And there still are Pascal Siakam, Aaron Nesmith, Obi Toppin, Andrew Nembhard, T.J. McConnell, plus the addition of Kelly Oubre.

Remember, two seasons ago the Pacers were a 50-win team and in the NBA Finals.

Yes, the team that went 5-0 last season against the Heat, with a returning core, is ranked below.

With Nikola Vucevic in for Moe Wagner, the Magic will stand as Exhibit A of how much a coaching change, alone, can change a culture.

It was an offseason of quality gained (Devin Carter, Lu Dort, Ryan Nembhard and Aaron Wiggins) and little of contribution lost (Jonathan Kuminga, Zaccharie Risacher).

It likely will come down to whether a defensive-driven roster can find enough scoring beyond Jalen Johnson. If Atlanta does, the win total could far exceed expectations.

title: Katie Taylor bows out as three-time undisputed champion
description: Katie Taylor brought her remarkable boxing career to a close in front of 80,000 jubilant fans at Croke Park, bowing out as a three-time undisputed world champion.The Bray native produced a dominant pe...
fullText:
Katie Taylor brought her remarkable boxing career to a close in front of 80,000 jubilant fans at Croke Park, bowing out as a three-time undisputed world champion.

The Bray native produced a dominant performance against unbeaten Flora Pili, securing a points victory to claim the vacant WBC light-welterweight title and complete an extraordinary final chapter.

Taylor finishes her career with 26 victories from 27 professional contests, having established herself as one of Ireland's greatest sporting figures.

The 40-year-old's farewell in Dublin was a night of celebration, spectacle and music, with Croke Park providing a fitting stage for the final appearance of a fighter who has transformed women's boxing.

And among the many supporters celebrating Taylor's achievements were Leeds United fans, with the former Republic of Ireland footballer having long spoken about her affection for the Whites.

Appearing on Soccer AM in 2019, Taylor revealed the origins of her Leeds connection.

"My team is actually Leeds United.

"My dad is from Leeds and my older two brothers grew up supporting Leeds as well. Every Christmas we would get Leeds jerseys for Christmas and football boots. I was a huge football fan growing up."

Taylor has previously described her visits to Elland Road as "some of my best memories as a kid", while her love of the club has remained throughout her hugely successful boxing career.

That connection was strengthened in 2021 when Taylor brought her world championship belts to Leeds, successfully defending her titles against Jennifer Han at Headingley Stadium.

Now, five years on from her night in Leeds, Taylor has called time on a career which saw her become a three-time undisputed world champion and one of the most influential figures in the history of women's sport.

Her final victory over Pili ensured she departed the sport on her own terms, adding another world title to a glittering collection before receiving the farewell she deserved in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park.

From the football pitches of Ireland to the biggest stages in boxing, Taylor's journey has been extraordinary.

And for Leeds United supporters, she will always be remembered as one of their own.

title: “Absolutely Robbed”: CFB Fans Feel For Western Michigan as Wolverines Win Low Scoring Thriller on Hail Mary
description: The Western Michigan Broncos almost pulled off an upset victory over the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. A low-scoring game in Ann Arbor left fans on the edge of their seats.
fullText:
The Western Michigan Broncos almost pulled off an upset victory over the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. A low-scoring game in Ann Arbor left fans on the edge of their seats.

In the fourth quarter, Western Michigan looked set for a huge upset after two field goals by Dieter Kelly. However, just before the final whistle, Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary attempt connected with wide receiver JJ Buchanan.

The clock appeared to have expired before the quarterback's previous throw. However, the officials put one second back after review, ruling that it touched an out-of-bounds Western Michigan defender. Underwood then connected with Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown to seal the win.

After the game, fans on social media reacted to Michigan's thrilling victory and Western Michigan's loss.

"Absolutely robbed," one fan wrote.

This victory marks the start of Kyle Whittingham's tenure as the coach of the Michigan Wolverines. He spent the past 21 seasons with the Utah Utes and posted a 177-88 overall record. In December, he agreed to a five-year deal to join Michigan as Sherrone Moore's replacement.

After the game, Kyle Whittingham had an interview with Big Ten Network on the field. When asked to share his thoughts on the victory, he praised his players for their resilience.

"Obviously, unbelievable last play," Whittingham said. "The defense played well, didn't allow a touchdown the entire game. We just hung in there.

"Fortunately, we had one second left on the clock. Bryce threw a perfect ball, JJ made a great catch. It's one for the history books right here."

Whittingham and his team next face the Oklahoma Sooners on Sept. 12 at noon ET.

title: Ajit Agarkar attends Duleep Trophy final at Chepauk: India's chief selector attends South Zone vs East Zone game days after missing BCCI review meeting
description: Chief selector Ajit Agarkar attended the Duleep Trophy 2026 final at Chepauk, days after missing BCCI's review meeting in Mumbai amid contract extension talks.
fullText:
Ajit Agarkar attends Duleep Trophy final at Chepauk: India's chief selector attends South Zone vs East Zone game days after missing BCCI review meeting originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar attended Day 1 of the Duleep Trophy final in Chennai days after missing the BCCI review meeting.

BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia confirmed no discussion about Agarkar's future took place during Thursday's review meeting in Mumbai.

The final doubles as an India A audition, with Mohammed Siraj and Devdutt Padikkal added for star power.

Ajit Agarkar turned up in person at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai to watch the Duleep Trophy 2026 final unfold on Day 1. The chief selector was spotted in the stands as South Zone took on East Zone in the summit clash on Sunday, September 6, putting to rest much of the speculation that had built up around his absence from Thursday's BCCI review meeting.

The 48-year-old wasn't at the BCCI gathering in Mumbai three days ago, and that absence, particularly given how much scrutiny surrounds his own future as chief selector, had lit up the rumour mill. There were even reports that the BCCI is looking for a new chief selector and his contract won't be extended beyond September.

MORE: End of Agarkar era: BCCI reportedly looking for new chief selector, board denies talks - Report

However, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia had moved to cool things down at the time, explaining that the meeting was called at very short notice and Agarkar simply wasn't in town.

"He was out of station. He could not be a part of the meeting because this meeting was called at very short notice, and our head of the selection committee, Ajit, was not in town, so he could not join it. He was in such an area that he could not join online, in spite of our best efforts," the BCCI secretary told reporters.

The board secretary also went out of his way to shut down any suggestions that Agarkar's future had been debated behind closed doors. Addressing reporters, he made the focus of Thursday's gathering clear: the England and Ireland tour performances, the recent Test series in Sri Lanka, the upcoming schedule, and the 2027 World Cup roadmap were the items on the table.

"There was no such discussion in today's meeting. There was no discussion on the selection committee. Our whole focus was performance in England and Ireland, as well as the recent Test series in Sri Lanka and what we are going to do in the upcoming series, plus the World Cup, which is our ultimate goal," Saikia said.

Head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, and T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer were all part of that gathering.

Agarkar's attendance at the final isn't just a formality or to shut down the rumour mill. This match carries significance as India have five 'A' Test matches coming up over the next two months, against Australia at home and New Zealand away.

The Duleep Trophy final is being treated as a key audition for players pushing for those spots, and Agarkar is at Chepauk specifically to run the eye over the contenders.

To make the occasion a bit more compelling, the BCCI added some popular names to the South Zone squad. Mohammed Siraj and Devdutt Padikkal were both brought in, while KL Rahul was approached but made himself unavailable.

His presence at Chepauk sends a message that the selection process is functioning, that eyes are on the right places, and that the India A pipeline is being monitored at the highest level. That's what the job demands, and he's delivering on it quietly but visibly.

title: Texas A&M looks to end its College GameDay struggles in 2026
description: Texas A&M faces a long-standing struggle to win when ESPN's College GameDay visits College Station, losing to right the ship under HC Mike Elko.
fullText:
Texas A&M kicked off the 2026 regular season against Missouri State on Saturday night, and while starting the season off 1-0 was fully expected, one of third-year coach Mike Elko's remaining challenges that has haunted the program for 20-plus seasons resurfaced this week before the season opener, as ESPN's College GameDay's nine appearances in College Station have been disastrous.

Since 2000, Texas A&M is just 1-8 when College GameDay made its way to College Station, with the first loss coming against No. 1 Oklahoma 35-31, while the only win came during the 2016 season when the Aggies defeated visiting Tennessee 45-38 in double overtime, which happens to be one of the most exciting finishes in recent memory.

Since that victory, the Jimbo Fisher era has been equally disappointing after six seasons, while the lone College GameDay loss to Clemson during Fisher's first season at the helm was a game that could, and should have, gone the other way if it weren't for several avoidable performances.

During Mike Elko's inaugural season, Texas A&M's loss to rival Texas at the end of the 2024 season wasn't a shock given the talent differential, while the Aggies' first-round loss to Miami in the first round of the College Football Playoff was by far the most disappointing defeat with College GameDay in town.

When the lights are brightest, Texas A&M must respond if the Aggies want to be taken seriously as a program truly building and contending for national titles, and while the 2025 season was certainly a solid start, expectations are even higher in 2026. If College GameDay makes its way back to College Station, it's time to change the narrative.

title: Commanders WR has one word to describe offense vs. Eagles in Week 1
description: Washington wide receiver Jaylin Lane on what to expect in Week 1 vs. Eagles.
fullText:
More than a few young athletes have gone to the NFL, NBA, MLB and talk about what they are going to do. They make it sound easy. You know why? Because they think it will be easier than it will be. They have not yet gained enough professional experience to understand how much more competitive things are professionally.

That might be the case with Washington Commanders' receiver/punt returner Jaylin Lane. Oh, he has exhibited a very sincere nature. He seems like a genuine young man. So he certainly has good intentions. But he did tell Scott Abraham this week, "I just think how we attack every day at practice. At the end of the day, this is the only sport where you practice more than you play."

Uh oh, Lane apparently has no idea how many hours swimmers spend in the pool each week, much more than during a swim meet. There's not a golfer who made it successfully to the PGA Tour that didn't spend hundreds of hours on the range, working on their short game, finally to have the opportunity to play in a tournament.

"Your days at practice leading up to the game, they got to be really good. And I think this is a really good week for us because yesterday we had a great day. Today we came out and attacked. So I think we are just, you know, ramping up to get ready."

I caught up with Commanders second year WR Jaylin Lane after today's practice.

About the David Blough offense that will be unleashed against the Eagles, Jaylin told me, "it's going to be explosive...I'm excited." pic.twitter.com/L7s9Ax5ZBk

When Abraham asked, "What is this offense going to be like?" Lane quickly responded, "Yeah, it's going to be explosive! We got a lot of explosive guys on the field. And Blough and the rest of the offensive side, they've been putting us in great positions to use our explosiveness. So, expect an explosive offense. I'm excited."

I'm glad Lane is excited; I'm glad he really likes OC David Blough's offense and coaching. I hope he's up to the challenge of NFL defenses. In the Commanders' first game, the offense will face the Eagles' defense. In the third week, they will face the Seahawks defense, which led Seattle to a Super Bowl Championship in 2025.

Hope Lane can have his own success this season.

title: Bill Madden: Tampa Bay Rays ready to usher in new era with stadium relocation near
description: NEW YORK — For years baseball people have marveled at the Tampa Bay Rays’ ability to remain competitive in the American League East despite consistently low industry payrolls and annual attendance. Since 2008, the Rays have been to the postseason nine times, including the World Series twice, always with payrolls of well over $100 million less than the Yankees. At the same time, Tampa Bay fans ...
fullText:
NEW YORK — For years baseball people have marveled at the Tampa Bay Rays' ability to remain competitive in the American League East despite consistently low industry payrolls and annual attendance. Since 2008, the Rays have been to the postseason nine times, including the World Series twice, always with payrolls of well over $100 million less than the Yankees.

At the same time, Tampa Bay fans have gotten used to the Rays' jettisoning their favorite players (See: Isaac Paredes, Randy Arozarena, Brandon Lowe and Tyler Glasnow in just the last three years) as soon as they became too costly or near free agency. And with the clock continuing to tick on their expiring (2028) lease at dreary Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla., there's never been a sense of permanence of the Rays in Tampa Bay.

Recently, both the Tampa city council and the Hillsborough County commissioners voted to approve a new $2.3 billion mixed-use stadium project near Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry Boulevard campus, not far from Raymond James Stadium, the home of the NFL Tampa Bay Bucs. The plan is similar to what the Atlanta Braves constructed in Cobb County, Ga., in 2015 for a stadium surrounded by a village of shops and restaurants that would produce addition revenue for the team.

It was always the accepted view of most folks in the Tampa Bay area that if the Rays were going to survive they would have to be in Tampa where the large majority of their 3 1/2 million residents are. This was part of the reason the Rays have remained one of the top revenue sharing recipients in baseball, an average of nearly $60 million a year. That's on top of the $50 million they and the other 29 clubs receive annually from the MLB Central Fund. So they've had the money to increase payroll, but the previous Rays owner Stu Sternberg just chose not to spend it.

If the owners are able to establish a cap in the new collective bargaining agreement, revenue sharing would go away, but the Rays are anticipating revenues of far more than $60 million from the new park and surrounding village which is now slated to be ready by 2029. For sure, now that the stadium issue has finally been resolved, the Rays, under their new ownership led by Jacksonville developer Patrick Zalupski, are expected to be operating vastly different. Last week Zalupski told the Tampa Bay Times: "Tampa's the No. 11 media market in the country. There's nothing holding it back, "adding that with the new ballpark and the development around it, "we should be able to drive payroll (currently 27th at $116,208,358) into the top 15 circle and maybe even the top 10."

In the meantime, the Rays have been leading the American League East since June 27, but will be facing their biggest challenge now in the September stretch, starting with this present road trip through Texas where they snapped a 10-game skid at Globe Life Field as of Friday, and three in Atlanta against the Braves. They then finish the season with three games with the Red Sox, four in New York with the Yankees and three more at home with the Phillies.

That four-game series at Yankee Stadium Sept. 22-24 figures to be the biggest regular-season series for both the Rays and the Yankees in years, especially since the Yankees expect to be (Aaron Judge) whole, while Rays GM Eric Neander made significant upgrades to his pitching at the trade deadline with Freddy Peralta from the Mets and hard-throwing righty reliever Tyler Wells from the Orioles, and in perhaps the best acquisition of all, filled the Rays longstanding need — a catcher who can hit — by landing Liam Hicks from the Marlins

If the Rays are able to emerge through that gauntlet still atop the AL East it should be cause for considerable concern for the Yankees. Because as improved as they've become this year, they figure to be this good and better for years to come with one of the top player development systems in baseball with a half dozen top 100 prospects including outfielders Theo Gillen, Jake Melton and Austin Overn and catcher Caden Bodine, all of whom could be making their debuts at some point next year.

In every way, the baseball future couldn't be brighter in Tampa Bay.

title: Padovano thinks Juventus v AC Milan will be a better game than previously

fullText:
Juventus take on AC Milan in Serie A this weekend in one of the most anticipated matches in European football, and the Old Lady will be eager to ensure the fixture lives up to its billing.

Juve have several top players in their squad. At the same time, Milan also have plenty of quality, so there is every reason to expect an entertaining contest between two teams with managers who will be determined to win.

In recent times, meetings between these sides have often been disappointing, with the Bianconeri primarily focused on ensuring they did not lose. Their cautious approach has contributed to some uninspiring encounters, but Juventus will want to take a different approach this time.

The Old Lady are expected to target a victory rather than simply trying to avoid defeat. Ruben Amorim will also want to win the fixture as he looks to ensure his team's fine start to the season continues.

One of these teams could surrender their winning run by the end of the match, and Juve will certainly not want to be the side that fails to maintain their momentum.

The Bianconeri have started the season with ambition and will see this fixture as another opportunity to demonstrate their quality. Facing Milan will provide a serious test, but Juventus will believe they have enough talent to secure the result they want.

Milan will have similar ambitions, meaning both sides should have plenty of motivation to attack the game. That could make this meeting very different from some of their recent encounters, particularly if neither team is willing to settle for a draw.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Michele Padovano also expects the fixture to be a good one and believes both teams have reasons to be optimistic about their progress. He said via Tuttojuve:

"Juventus-Milan will be a great match, because they are two teams that intrigue me more than anyone else: Juve have had a top-notch transfer window and have invested in areas where they were most needed, while I had a great impression of Amorim's play from the Rossoneri. I see both of them improving compared to previous years; they will certainly be able to reverse the negative trend."

Padovano's comments underline the excitement surrounding both teams. Juventus and Milan will now look to prove that their progress can translate into a strong performance when they meet in Serie A today.

title: How Buffon is moving on from the ‘searing disappointment’ of Italy’s World Cup
description: Italy legend Gianluigi Buffon admits he tries to ‘eliminate negative experiences from his mind,’ including Italy’s latest elimination from the World Cup play-off: ‘The only penalties I revisit...
fullText:
Italy legend Gianluigi Buffon admits he tries to 'eliminate negative experiences from his mind,' including Italy's latest elimination from the World Cup play-off: 'The only penalties I revisit in my sleep are those from the triumph in Berlin in 2006.'

Buffon was Italy's delegation chief this past March when the Azzurri, under coach Gennaro Gattuso, faced elimination in the World Cup play-off final, losing on penalties to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

PARIS, FRANCE – SEPTEMBER 06: Gianluigi Buffon of Italy attends before the UEFA Nations League 2024/25 League A Group A2 match between France and Italy at Parc des Princes stadium on September 06, 2024 in Paris, France. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

The loss marked Italy's third consecutive failure to qualify for the World Cup, but Buffon no longer dwells on it.

"No, because I have a great ability to eliminate sad and negative experiences from my mind," he told Gazzetta.

"I am optimistic and naturally confident, which is probably why the only penalties I revisit in my sleep are those from the triumph in Berlin in 2006. The one in Bosnia was a deep and searing disappointment, but my way of living and surviving these burns is to overcome them with something beautiful and majestic."

ZENICA, BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA – MARCH 31: Haris Tabakovic of Bosnia and Herzegovina scores his team's equalizing goal during the FIFA World Cup 2026 European Qualifiers KO play-offs match between Bosnia & Herzegovina and Italy at Stadion Bilino Polje on March 31, 2026 in Zenica, Bosnia and Herzegovina. (Photo by Getty Images/Getty Images)

Buffon stepped down from his role following Italy's exit, and the same did coach Gattuso and FIGC President Gabriele Gravina.

During the same interview, Buffon previewed tonight's big game between Juventus and Milan, claiming that the Bianconeri have a slight advantage over the Rossoneri.

title: Three reasons Wisconsin shocks the world vs. Notre Dame in Week 1
description: The Wisconsin Badgers are finally looking to kickstart things under head coach Luke Fickell, who enters his fourth full season with the program.
fullText:
The Wisconsin Badgers are finally looking to kickstart things under head coach Luke Fickell, who will soon be entering his fourth full season with the program.

While things aren't completely dire, if the Badgers show another year of regression under the former Cincinnati coach, then his reign may come to an end.

However, all of that can change with a strong 2026 season. Overall, the Badgers have a workable schedule that sees them missing out on playing against Oregon, Michigan, Ohio State, or Indiana. All they have to do is start things right against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish, who come into the season ranked No. 4 in the AP Poll and No. 5 in the US LBM Coaches Poll.

Today's task is to look at the three reasons why this upset is on the cards

The Irish struggle to close out games prior to October, with their only two losses last season occurring before September 14, and who could forget their shock loss to the Northern Illinois Huskies the season prior. It's not quite known why the first few weeks of the season generate a slow start, but it is clear that if there is a time to face them, it's sooner rather than later.

It has been a long time since a Wisconsin backfield has looked as promising as it does with Sama and Joseph. During his time in the Big 12, Sama compiled four games where he rushed for over 100 yards. Joseph leaves Old Dominion with nine games of at least 250 passing yards and four games of at least 100 rushing yards in his career, so it's clear these two can single-handedly take games by the scruff of the neck if the Irish aren't careful.

It is easy to remember all of the faults last year's offense compiled, but it is harder to remember that despite facing seven teams ranked inside the AP Top 25, the Badgers only allowed 323.6 yards per game, good enough for 23rd-best in the country. With transfers like safety Marvin Burks Jr. and the Irish's ability to start off slow, the Badgers' defense could find ways to break the game open.

title: Start with one customer
description:
If you’ve been into side projects, you’ve probably seen countless times the story of someone building something really big and complex, launching it, and having 0 users. With the AI era we’re living in, this will become even more common since software is cheaper to make.
I’ve worked on many side projects over the years, some with big ambitions and some very small, to solve a specific personal challenge. And that’s fine, I love to work on something that allows me to be fully creative without restrictions, but if your goal is to create a business, the starting place needs to be a bit different.
fullText:
If you’ve been into side projects, you’ve probably seen countless times the story of someone building something really big and complex, launching it, and having 0 users. With the AI era we’re living in, this will become even more common since software is cheaper to make.

I’ve worked on many side projects over the years, some with big ambitions and some very small, to solve a specific personal challenge. And that’s fine, I love to work on something that allows me to be fully creative without restrictions, but if your goal is to create a business, the starting place needs to be a bit different.

Instead of working for months and launching something, thinking you can be really big and have thousands of random people all over the world using your product, start with one person. The auto repair shop owner down the street, a lawyer you know, the restaurant manager, a teacher at your kids’ school. Start with that particular person and their specific challenges, and think of ways you can address them.

Perhaps they don’t need your service or SaaS software for that, but if it makes their lives easier in any way (saving time or money, or making them feel better), you have a business opportunity.

Build something with that person in mind, watch very closely how they operate, and start using your first version, and then, once a couple of months have passed, start expanding. Ask colleagues, talk to other people in that sector, and see who else might be interested.

If you’ve been able to help one person, you can help two, and three.

Things take time, of course, but if this is a side project, you have time on your side; there’s no VC asking for growth charts.

A small piece of strategic advice: start with the marketing side as soon as possible. Landing page, social content, SEO… They take time to show up on Google and other places, so the sooner you start, the better.

At some point, people will start looking for your solution and finding you, rather than the other way around. At that point, congratulations! You have a business.

title: Changing the world one vegetable at a time: UK first carbon-negative greengrocer
description: I spent a day with the UK's first carbon-negative greengrocers who are changing the future for generations to come, right here in Leicester
fullText:
This story was published by the Leicester Gazette: a local, independent newspaper about Leicestershire. 1,000 people have already joined our mailing list. Just use that button below to 

No spam. Unsubscribe anytime. Want to support our work? Click here for membership.

Leicester is associated with many great things: its cultural quarter, the space industry, and its dynamic culinary scene, to name a few. But in the city there’s innovation happening quietly, one delivery at a time. I recently learned that Leicester is home to the UK's first carbon-negative mobile greengrocers. I was in the middle of renovating my Clarendon Park flat – and was caked in sawdust – when I saw it: a brilliantly decorated 1950s milk float, with fruit and vegetables instead of milk, and the words ‘slow-moving veg’ written on the back.

Naturally, in a disheveled state, I walked up to the driver, told him I was a reporter, and expressed my interest in writing about them. I got a business card in return. In the weeks that followed, my editor green-lit a feature on the greengrocer, and I set a date for an interview. What followed was probably one of the most pleasant Friday mornings I’ve had in a long time, as I joined the Green Tomato team on one of their routes around Stoneygate.

I arrive at the home of the Green Tomato founders, husband and wife team Nisha and Manoj. One of their employees, Callum, is there – he’s back from a 4am trip to Leicester's wholesale market, and has helped load the float, which is parked outside on the driveway.

Before we even set off, the community feel which the Green Tomato is built around is evident: “hey mate,” shouts a postman as he power-walks across the road. He hands Manoj a couple of letters and the two chat briefly about the weather. Then, as he turns to leave, Manoj hands him an apple from the float. “It’s his favourite apple,” Nisha later tells me when I ask her about it.

So we hit the road, and less than five minutes later we’ve arrived at our first stop in Stoneygate, and the first customer opens their front door, reusable carrier bags in hand. I learn that his name is Stuart.

Once Stuart has finished his shopping, I ask him: “How long have you shopped with the Green Tomato?”

“Since Covid days, wasn’t it?” He asks Manoj – who nods in response, “Six years now, it’s going to be six years in July.

“And I’m still only 53,” he says, which is met with chuckles from Manoj and Nisha.

I ask him about Leicester Market as well, and why he doesn't shop there. “I don’t go into central Leicester, I’m retired,” he responds. “I visit Boots to have my eyes and ears tested, and that’s about the only time I go in.”

But anyway, “this is a great local business”, he says. And with that, Stuart heads back into his house, carrier bags of produce in hand.

The float departs, and snakes its way through the streets of Stoneygate, stopping to make deliveries as we go. As Manoj fills his customers’ bags with fresh produce, they chat away about all sorts. He's well aware of what's going on in his customers’ lives, and they discuss topics ranging from customers' families to holidays (Manoj and Nisha are going to Türkiye and will be missed dearly by their customers) and, in keeping with the older demographic of the customers on this particular route, various age-related medical topics. The relationship between the Green Tomato and its customer base is a close one, and the conversations are reminiscent of catchup between friends rather than a vendor and a buyer.

On this particular route, most of the customers are retirees, Nisha tells me. But the Green Tomatoes' other routes through Clarendon Park and Knighton attract customers of all ages.

We pull up outside the front door of another regular. “Manoj is a treasure – write that down,” he tells me, after he’s finished shopping. He’s a retired professor with a characterful received accent. “He is the best thing that’s ever happened to me; there’s lots of people – like me – who can’t get out to get fresh fruit and veg.” The Green Tomato is “absolutely marvellous,” as far as he is concerned.

Convenience is the main draw for customers in Stoneygate, “it’s somebody coming to your door, and it’s a personal service,” says one. “It’s the human touch – that’s the most important thing,” says another.

After the route had ended, Nisha and I spent around 20 minutes chatting about the Green Tomato.

“We have family in India and every time we visit, the best part of our visit is where the stall comes,” she says. “It’s pulled by a person normally, and it's got fresh produce from local farms.  There’s no packaging.”

She continues, “nobody in India goes to do their fresh food shop in a supermarket. It's not a thing. Nobody does that.

“It's frustrating that people are not doing more; there's so much evidence now of human activity and the impact on our environment, and yet behaviour change is difficult. I thought this would actually kill two birds with one stone. By bringing the shop to the doorstep, we're going to be zero emissions.”

The Green Tomato has three separate routes: one in Knighton, one in Clarendon Park, and one in Stoneygate. Something to note is that these are nice areas of Leicester, known for being desirable places to live which are pretty well-off (the Guardian wrote 14 years ago of ‘corduroyed lecturers in cafés’ and ‘legendary cheeseboards’ in Clarendon Park and that certainly still rings true today).

This is something I wanted to ask about, but I'm beaten to the punch when Nisha says, “Our suppliers are brilliant, but the cost of our buying is more than the supermarket prices. So, although we want the business to be accessible to everyone, in fact, it's just not turned out like that.”

At the end of the day, the Green Tomato is a business, and “We need to remain profitable to do all the things that we do,” says Nisha. “We've ended up with a very niche customer base, which we're fully aware of. But we want to open up to everyone, and that will involve help.”

What that help looks like isn’t yet clear to the Tomato, but Nisha assures me that expanding the business and reaching more customers is high up on their agenda. Some support may come from councils or from charities. “One of the targets for local councils is to be able to provide fresh fruit and veg in certain areas where it's difficult,” says Nisha. It’s early days yet, and while talks are happening and Nisha has “made a few inroads,” there’s not yet a solid plan in place that she’s ready to share with me.

One thing I’m struck by is the sense of community the Green Tomato has managed to build. I’ve reported previously on Leicester Market, and have had traders speak to me extensively about the value of community. It seems it doesn't matter if you're on a stall or on the streets, that community is fuelling independent small businesses throughout the city.

Before you go… We’ve recently surpassed 1,000 subscribers, which is amazing considering we’re a small team on a shoestring budget.

Now, we’re ready for the next stage of the Leicester Gazette. Download our new app and get all of our journalism anytime, anywhere.

The app connects with Bluesky, Mastodon and Threads, giving you access to a network of around 60 million people. It’s a safer, more meaningful alternative to mainstream social media – owned by the community.

title: Is Bain on course to be Scotland's number one?
description: With Sebastien Pocognoli looking to change the way Scotland play, might Scott Bain be the answer to his goalkeeping problems?
fullText:
Eight saves, many of them excellent. Good distribution. And a man of the match performance. If timing is everything, Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain may just have played his way into the forefront of the new Scotland head coach's thinking.

Sebastien Pocognoli will soon be announcing his first squad for the forthcoming Nations League games.

With the retirement of Craig Gordon and the lack of recent first-team minutes for Angus Gunn and Liam Kelly - the other two World Cup squad goalkeepers - is Bain the obvious answer to Pocognoli's potential problem?

On the evidence of his display in the 1-1 draw against Dundee United on Saturday - without which his side may well have been beaten given the number of chances United created - he'll be very unlucky not to be recalled to the international fold.

Unsurprisingly, Bain's manager John McGlynn was happy to sing his praises.

"I thought he was terrific," McGlynn said of the 34-year-old, who has earned four caps over the past eight years.

"If you're looking for a goalkeeper who can play from the back and still make saves and bring composure and calmness to your defence, then I think Scott ticks all the boxes. So I have no doubt that the manager will be looking at him."

Stoppage-time concession denies Falkirk first win

Latest Falkirk news, analysis and fan views

There will be a number of Dundee United players cursing Bain's name after Saturday's game.

Full-back Kevin Ciubotaru's shot seemed destined for the bottom right-hand corner before Bain intervened. United debutant Lyall Cameron also watched in anguish as Bain denied him.

Another new boy, Zidane Iqbal, arrowed a shot towards the top corner only for Bain to tip it away. And the goalkeeper thwarted Neil Farrugia, too.

It was a heroic display of defiance that very nearly earned his side a first league win of the season, but for Michael Forbes' stoppage-time header.

After a mistake at Celtic Park last weekend, Bain was back to his best.

United assistant manager Lee Sharp was also quick to praise Bain's contribution and agree that he's done his Scotland chances absolutely no harm whatsoever.

"Absolutely," he said. "He had two or three really good saves in the second half."

That was perhaps an understatement. Falkirk faced 27 shots, nine of which were on target. All of which were repelled by Bain until the late leveller.

He has now played 44 games for Falkirk, keeping 10 clean sheets in the process. He kept the ball out of the net in half of his 78 games for Celtic prior to that.

At Dundee, Bain's stats were pretty good, too - 21 clean sheets in 124 games.

Alex McLeish gave him his Scotland debut against Mexico in June 2018, after which he played a further three times for his country. His last cap came against Ivory Coast in a pre-World Cup friendly in March but he did not make the finals squad.

On his current form, he'll have every right to hope there's a new lease of international life coming in Pocognoli's brave new vision for Scotland.

title: Unruly passenger arrested after being restrained with duct tape during flight
description: The plane to Newark was diverted to Baltimore due to the disturbance.
fullText:
A man was arrested for alleged unruly behavior on an American Airlines flight causing it to divert to Baltimore on Thursday night, according to the airline and investigators.

Arthur Lundeen, 67, of Arizona, was restrained to his seat with duct tape and his hands were restrained with zip ties, according to the Maryland Transportation Authority Police, which arrested him after the plane landed.

The incident took place on American Airlines flight AA 618, which took off from Dallas and was en route to Newark, according to the FBI and the airline.

Juan Mejia, a passenger on that flight and a former law enforcement officer, told ABC he began hearing a disturbance about three quarters of the way into the flight.

"[The] gentleman sitting two rows behind us started becoming belligerent, making derogatory remarks to the staff of American Airlines and other passengers, racial slurs, vulgar language, very offensive to the women" sitting in the row behind the man, Mejia said.

Mejia and his friend Richard Olenick, who were on board the flight, told ABC they were monitoring the situation and intervened after they claimed Lundeen became physical.

"Juan immediately knew that action had to be taken. He got up right away and jumped in the seat right next to the passenger and began working on restraining him in order to keep the situation contained," Olenick told ABC.

Unruly passenger detained after incident on Delta flight, police say

Authorities did not provide details of the disruption that took place during the flight, but the plane was diverted to Baltimore Washington International (BWI) Airport around 10:15 p.m., the Federal Aviation Administration, which is also probing the incident, said.

The two passengers said they stayed with Lundeen until law enforcement officials boarded the plane and took him into custody after they landed in Baltimore.

"We weren't looking to hurt this individual; we were looking more to restrain him and control him, so it didn't escalate to go any further," Mejia said.

Lundeen was removed from the plane and the flight continued to Newark, American Airlines said in a statement.

Lundeen was charged with disorderly conduct and second-degree assault "for incidents that occurred aboard the aircraft at BWI Airport," the MDTA Police said.

The reported incident that took place in the air is being investigated by the FBI.

"Lundeen was cleared by paramedics for an open wound on his arm that was noticed by officers while being taken into custody," the MTDA Police said in a statement.

"The safety ​and ​security ​of our customers ​and team members ​is our top ​priority and ​we ​do not ​tolerate violence," American Airlines said in a statement.

Video United flight diverted after alleged unruly passenger incident

The FBI said the investigation is ongoing.

ABC News' Jack Date contributed to this report.

title: Wigan crush Leeds to move closer to winning shield
description: Wigan Warriors move within touching distance of winning the League Leaders' Shield after a superb victory at closest rivals Leeds Rhinos.
fullText:
Tries: Keighran 3, Daniel, Marshall, French, Field Goals: Keighran 6

Wigan Warriors produced an outstanding display on the big occasion once again as they defeated Leeds Rhinos to take a giant step towards lifting the League Leaders' Shield.

The Warriors leapfrogged the Rhinos to move two points clear at the top and if they match Leeds' result in the final game of the regular season on Friday, they will claim their second piece of silverware of the year.

It was their 14th straight Super League win and it is hard to imagine them not beating Catalans Dragons at home to finish the job, with the Rhinos welcoming Hull FC at the same time.

Two early tries from Adam Keighran put them in charge at a sold-out Headingley before Ash Handley got Leeds on the scoreboard before the break.

Teenage winger Austin Daniel scored only his second Super League try to restore a 10-point advantage before fellow winger Liam Marshall crossed early in the second half to put Wigan firmly in control.

Their defence remained resolute as Leeds tried to get back into the game, and further tries from star backs Bevan French and Jai Field and a hat-trick from Keighran showed why they will be strong favourites to win the Grand Final at Old Trafford on 3 October.

Wakefield stay in top-four hunt with win over Wire

York run in five tries for dream win over Catalans

Women's Super League: Wigan thrash Leeds to storm on

The Rhinos have been top since May in pursuit of their first silverware since 2020 – a long wait for one of rugby league's powerhouses - while they have not finished top of Super League since 2015.

But the Warriors have been in their rearview mirror as they have been imperious through the summer, on the back of a winning streak which started more than three months ago with a dismantling of Hull KR in the Challenge Cup final at Wembley.

After a shaky spring, Wigan have been back to their best as they chase a treble, to go with the quadruple they secured two years ago.

Super League's leading try scorer, Maika Sivo, did not make the Leeds squad after recovering from a broken arm, but there was a setback for the hosts early in the game as full-back Lachie Miller limped off with a hamstring injury.

With the Rhinos reshuffling, Wigan pounced as the great teams do. Sharp handling from French and Keighran got the ball to 19-year-old Daniel who, on just his fourth league appearance, showed a turn of pace down the wing and then awareness to set up Keighran to score.

Oliver Partington had a try disallowed, but the Warriors were not to be denied as French's bullet pass put fellow Australian Keighran over again.

Leeds were stunned but found a response as Connor hoisted a high kick which was brilliantly caught and then touched down by captain Handley.

They were right back in the contest, but French simply dipped into his box of tricks to move Wigan further clear as the stand-off threw a sensational pass that took out three defenders and gave Daniel a walk-in.

Connor kicked a goal on the stroke of half-time to reduce the gap to eight points. But the visitors claimed the first score of the second half through Marshall's trademark finish in the left corner, although the unhappy hosts believed Wigan had knocked on in the build-up.

There was a hint of desperation as Leeds tried to force their way back into the game, but there were no chinks in the Warriors defence and their class was on show at the other end.

Harry Smith's clever kick found space and French, on his 200th career appearance, was first on to it, before Field's dazzling feet grabbed Wigan's sixth try.

Keighran then completed his hat-trick as the clock was ticking down to cap another glorious night for this storied club.

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur told BBC Radio Leeds:

"We're disappointed, we didn't put our best foot forward tonight. It was a big occasion for the club and not through effort, but we let ourselves down and we let the club down.

"It's certainly not over, but we've got to dust ourselves down. We've got a big game next week and we need to regain some form.

On Lachlan Miller's injury: "It's not great. He's obviously got to go and have scans, but I think he's torn his hamstring. We'll have to wait and see.

"It's hard to replace a player of his quality, but then it's hard to replace a full-back, they're so integral to your defensive line, the organisation of that and how he returns the ball.

"We were a bit disjointed from it, but we've got to be a bit more resilient."

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told BBC Radio Manchester:

"I was pleased with the performance. I knew we were coming up against a really good team - a great arena, the build-up, the crowd.

"We knew it was going to be a big occasion, so to get the job done, I'm pleased, I'm proud.

"Leeds get the basics of the game right and challenge you in so many ways, so concentration is a big one and then embracing the big occasion. These are the sorts of games you want to be involved in as players.

"We played well, Leeds will learn a lot. They were unfortunate with the injury at the start, they've got some players to come back, they'll go away and come back better I'm sure, so we have to be prepared to keep improving as well."

Leeds: Miller; Hall, Bird, Handley, Newman; Croft, Connor; Oledzki, O'Connor, Jenkins, Watkins, Hankinson, Cassell.

Interchanges: C Smith, Lodge, Lloyd, Holroyd.

Wigan: Field; Daniel, Keighran, Eckersley, Marhsall; French, H Smith; Havard, O'Neill, Thompson, McDermott, Partington, Ellis.

title: Hunt 'not afraid of anyone' after second podium in two days
description: Amy Hunt says she is "on the up" and "not afraid of anyone" after finishing second in the 100m at the Diamond League final in Brussels.
fullText:
Amy Hunt says she is "on the up" and "not afraid of anyone" after finishing second in the 100m at the Diamond League final in Brussels.

The 24-year-old Briton finished in 11.06 seconds, behind Jamaica's Tina Clayton who won in 10.93, just one day after a third-placed finish in the 200m.

Hunt's performance surpassed American Olympic silver medallist Sha'Carri Richardson, who came third in 11.07.

It continues Hunt's fine late season form after winning four gold medals at the European Championships in Birmingham last month.

"I am 24 and on the up and up and up. I am not afraid of the other girls," said Hunt.

"I have so much love and respect for them and they are absolute icons but I love the challenge of going head to head with them.

"It takes me back to younger days racing boys in the school playground."

Hunt is planning to compete in the 100m and 200m again at the inaugural Ultimate Championships event in Budapest, which begins on 11 September.

"To come away with two podiums is no mean feat, and I am the only athlete to double up in the sprints and I came away with a second and a third," added Hunt.

Fellow Briton Georgia Hunter Bell came fourth in the 1500m despite being among the pre-race favourites.

Hunter Bell has won three international titles this year, including the world indoor 1500m, Commonwealth Games 800m and European 1500m, but never looked like threatening the top three in Brussels.

Poland's Klaudia Kazimierska came first with a time of three minutes 54.05 seconds, with Kenya's Dorcus Ewoi second and Australia's Jessica Hull third.

Hunter Bell said her performance was a result of a "long hard season", with the 32-year-old having competed in 19 races this year.

"I have done three championships so I am starting to feel it in my body," said Hunter Bell.

"I am struggling a little bit, even mentally to get my adrenaline up again week in, week out, but I am really lucky to be racing and to be happy and healthy.

"I just have to regroup before the Ultimate Championships next week, but I have to be happy with my consistency this season."

Elsewhere, Switzerland's Audrey Werro won the women's 800m final but was pushed all the way by Dutch athlete Femke Broeders-Bol.

With British Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson missing through injury, Werro hung on during the final straight with Broeders-Bol at her heels.

Werro, who has set the third, fourth and fifth fastest 800m times in history this year, finished in 1:54.75, which was 0.06secs in front of Broeders-Bol.

Brazil's Alison dos Santos and America's Masai Russell, who set world records in the men's 400m hurdles and women's 100m hurdles last week respectively, repeated their victories in Brussels but could not better the times they set in Zurich.

fullText:
Sept 6 (Reuters) - The U.S. aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln left Thailand on Sunday after ‌a five-day port visit, ending a respite ‌from an extended deployment that included operations in the Middle ​East, the U.S. Navy said.

"We would like to thank the people of Thailand for their incredible hospitality," U.S. Navy Captain Dan Keeler, the Abraham Lincoln's commanding ‌officer, said in ⁠a statement.

Naval deployments typically last for six to nine months, but during times ⁠of conflict that can be extended.

The nuclear-powered Lincoln, with roughly 5,000 personnel, was involved in the ​U.S. naval ​blockade and combat ​operations in the war ‌with Iran and — according to Democratic lawmakers — set a modern-day record for consecutive days at sea.

Accompanied by other U.S. naval vessels, the Lincoln arrived early on Wednesday in Thailand, the United States' ‌only treaty partner in mainland ​Southeast Asia, during a visit ​that Thai officials ​said would last five days.

Busloads of ‌sailors and Marines wearing ​civilian clothes, many ​smiling and waving, started arriving at a hotel in the resort city of Pattaya, ​about 150 km (93 ‌miles) southeast of Bangkok, shortly after their ​ships docked.

title: Judge indicates Trump pressure campaign could permanently sink Reflecting Pool case
description: Asked whether prosecutors were investigating Hearn, they said they weren't.
fullText:
Former U.S. Olympian David Hearn and his attorneys returned to court to urge the judge who previously oversaw his Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool vandalism case to formally bar federal prosecutors from seeking new charges against him.

In late July, the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office moved to dismiss the criminal case against Hearn in a filing that acknowledged damage to the Reflecting Pool "was the result of flawed installation" and not the work of vandals -- prompting outrage from President Donald Trump.

But the motion from U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro asked the judge overseeing Hearn's case, Todd Edelman, to dismiss the indictment "without prejudice," which would leave the door open for prosecutors to potentially seek to re-charge Hearn.

Hearn's attorneys have argued a series of statements from Trump and other officials in the weeks after Pirro's motion that falsely accused him and others of vandalizing the pool warrants dismissal of the case "with prejudice" -- effectively shutting the door for prosecutors to charge him again.

DOJ seeks to keep door open to re-charge David Hearn in Reflecting Pool case

"U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro should re-visit her hastily made decision [to dismiss Hearn's indictment]," Trump said in an Aug. 7 post on social media.

In Friday's hearing, Judge Edelman pressed an attorney from Pirro's office, Michael Spence, on why prosecutors would object to dismissing the case with prejudice when they've received no evidence thus far suggesting anything Hearn did was a crime.

"I don't know what the future will bring -- none of us do," Spence answered, adding if evidence did ultimately surface, "there's no reason this court should tie the hands of a future grand jury to bring that indictment."

"Where is it gonna come from?" Edelman asked.

"That I don't know," Spence answered.

Former Olympian David Hearn's lawyers say Trump pushing 'false version' of Reflecting Pool case

When asked by Edelman whether prosecutors were still investigating Hearn's conduct, Spence said they were not.

"The U.S. Attorney's Office is not, no," Spence answered.

At one point, Edelman zeroed in on Trump's public comments about Hearn's case and his public suggestions he might fire Pirro if she doesn't revisit her decision to drop the case.

"How do I conclude these statements as anything other than statement by the chief executive urging your office to pursue a prosecution that you have told me is meritless?" Edelman pressed. "Isn't this a pretty unique threat of not just re-prosecution but meritless re-prosecution?"

"I think, Your Honor, it's premature to even get there because there has not -- this case has been dropped. It has not been submitted to a new grand jury for an indictment," Spence replied.

Former Olympian David Hearn's attorneys want Reflecting Pool vandalism case permanently dismissed

Spence argued that even if the government did at some point move to re-charge him, the grand jury process would serve as a kind of protection ensuring he wouldn't be charged based on no evidence.

"How could Mr. Hearn look at this case and make that conclusion?" Edelman asked with clear skepticism, noting Hearn was previously indicted in a case the government now concedes was baseless.

"We believed based on the evidence that we had at the time that we had probable cause, and the grand jury agreed that we did have probable cause," Spence answered.

title: Josh Sargent rises to occasion for TFC with first MLS hat-trick 🇺🇸
